# Session Summaries

## Pre-Session History \- Trouble Brews

Our story begins in *Barrow Spa*, the capital of *Barrowshire*, a spa town near an ancient burial site now teeming with undead. Recently, skeletons and other undead have begun attacking merchants and kidnapping travelers. Both an angry dwarf and a frightened merchant offered sums of gold to the party in exchange for their services.

Exploring the town, the group visited the *Steamy Smithy*, a spa-smith hybrid run by Agar and Esme. Continuing on, they met Amadeus Thud of the *Minimarket* along with his local one-eyed rat friend Spat. Finally, the group were made aware of a secure goods storage establishment named the *Lost Luggage*.

The party previously explored the *Barrow*, battling a carcass crawler at the cost of one ally being paralysed for the duration of the adventure. The group cautiously made their way to the central chamber and found the cause of the road’s banditry problem \- ten animated and very chatty skeletons. It seemed that they had been resurrected by a necromancer who was unable to control them and had been forced to promise that they would be restored to their human forms. 

Realising the skeletons were growing hostile, Virien caused a distraction \- a disembodied voice promising resurrection \- and the group dashed further into the dungeon, discovering Quintius. The necromancer explained that he had failed to deliver on his promises, angering his undead followers.

Under the promise of treasure, the group began to rush Quintius out of the dungeon \- only stopping briefly to free six imprisoned merchants along the way before they escorted everyone out of the *Barrow*, pursued by the enraged undead.

## Session 1 \- Into the Barrow

The group returns to town, heading to the opulent *Red Herring* inn, where Quintius gives the party his ruby amulet as thanks for his rescue and reveals secrets about the *Barrow*, including hidden chambers and a mysterious resident fairy. Virien and Barny are rewarded by the freed silk merchants, and new allies \- Arden, Malakai, Ike, and Karsin \- join the group, drawn by rumors of treasure and hatred of the undead.

The party ventures into the *Barrow*, its entrance ominously sealing behind them. After fending off a skeleton ambush, they uncover a marble slab marked with an ‘X,’ making enough noise while investigating to attract the carcass crawler. Karsin is paralyzed in the fight, but the group manages to slay the creature, with Barny harvesting its venom. Later, they encounter and burn a gigantic, sleeping black widow spider in its web \- Virien almost dying after accidentally stabbing himself with one of the beast’s fangs. Pressing on, they discover a narrow tunnel that could serve as an escape route. While Ike and Malakai scout ahead, a zombie sneaks up on the rest of the party. Malakai deals with it swiftly \- a bolt to the head. Though the party survives the dangers of the *Barrow*, they find no treasure and return to town to regroup.

## Session 2 \- Bones, Fairy Deals, and Fallen Friends

Back at *The Red Herring*, the party enlists the aid of a sarcastic fighter, Stan Nice. They visit the silk merchants to cash in their IOUs and are directed to *The Bean Counter*, a magical vegan cafe and cooperative bank. Ruby Sunbeam, the cafe’s owner, oversees the withdrawal, with pixies delivering a chest of gold, which the party promptly redeposits, earning an exasperated sigh. Armed with their bank ledger, the group recruits Grog, a gruff dwarf, and buys supplies, including a draft horse, a cart, and an alphorn, before returning to the Barrow.

Scouting around the Barrow reveals no new entrances. Grog is stationed at the entrance with the alphorn, but disaster strikes when the party explores a caved-in corridor. Stan is killed while reaching for a magical sword held by skeletal arms. Virien retrieves the \+1 sword after sustaining injuries, and they drag Stan’s body to the entrance, where a demoralized Grog abandons his post. The party positions their cart and horse inside the Barrow before pressing on.

In a chamber to the right, they free Alfwine, a grateful fairy trapped under a cairn, who says she will only help them if they pledge to aid her in eradicating the undead that imprisoned her. Together, they continue exploring but are ambushed in a storage room by skeletons. Arden is injured, and Ike is slain before the party dispatches the attackers. Mourning their loss, they push forward, discovering a room with three tapestries. Arden triggers a cloud of spores from Yellow Mould while trying to loot a tapestry but narrowly escapes harm. A hidden pulley and secret door behind the tapestries reveal a small chamber with a white marble idol surrounded by white, magical flames. Arden valiantly risks his life to retrieve three blue gems from the brazier, surviving the fire and claiming the adventure’s only treasure.

Down by two party members, they decide to leave. As they roll back the entrance stone, two zombies ambush them. In the chaos, Virien is killed, struck with his own alphorn, along with Alfwine, but the zombies are defeated by Barny and Arden. Weakened and grieving, the remaining party members leave the Barrow and return to town.

## Session 3 \- Barrow Blitz

Mourning their losses, Arden and Barny read the wills of their fallen comrades. Ike has no will, and Stan wishes to stay dead, but Virien requests a second chance at life, hoping not to disappoint his parents. Seeking resurrection, the pair finds two establishments: *The Second Chance* (offering Raise Dead for 1000GP) and *The Last Chance* (offering Reincarnation for 500GP). Knowing Virien’s frugality, they choose *The Last Chance*. In an unlikely stroke of luck, Virien is reincarnated back into his own body.

Reuniting with Karsin and Malakai, the party recruits new members: the cleric Ulrich, and several retainers, including Bran "The Wolf", Grog, Rhian, and Dreg, all hired with daily stipends and shares of treasure. After restocking supplies and naming themselves **The Bonebreakers**, they post a notice offering 7 gold to any adventurers who respond to a blast on the alphorn for aid at the *Barrow*.

Returning to the *Barrow*, Virien alters the antechamber’s curse inscription to “Beware: Bonebreakers Bullying Barrowlanders”. Shortly after, they encounter and defeat five skeletons, with Bran delivering a crushing blow and Virien cleverly luring more using his Ventriloquism spell. After the battle, Virien sets a trap with a string and bell to alert them to anyone coming from behind. Sneaking further, led by Malakai and Dreg, they find four rats in the tapestry room, which Arden safely lures away with rations. Pressing on, they retrieve two glass eyes from a room of empty coffers, retrospectively realizing they were the key to solving the idol’s puzzle.

They pass through previously explored areas, moving through the prison room, before finding Quintius’ decrepit room. They then enter the Barrow’s largest chamber. Inside, Virien confidently convinces a lone skeleton that he can bring it back to life. The skeleton, desperate to return to life, obeys his order, drinking holy water, and is destroyed. Securing the chamber, the party hauls a mass of treasure back to the entrance, including 500GP, 1000SP, gemstones, silk, wine, and an ivory drinking horn.

With Sirius the draft horse and their cart intact, the Bonebreakers return to town, laden with loot and excited to roam a new location in search of more treasure.

## Session 4 \- Gilded Gears and Grease Trails

![][image1]

Back in Barrow Spa, the Bonebreakers are summoned to the *Guildhall*, where Reginald, the self-important Guildmaster of Tourism Merchants, pleads for their aid. Travelers are vanishing along the *Kingsroad*, with rumors of a creature taking them. He offers 600 GP and two draft horses with a cart as reward for solving the issue. Virien and Arden argue the pay is too low, but the group accepts, hoping for greater treasures.

Before setting out, they visit *Pimp My Ride*, commissioning the tattooed ex-con-esque proprietor, Gus, to paint their cart black with red lettering for 875 GP. They sell treasures, stock up on supplies, and Ulrich buys a hunting dog, Fred. A group of rookie adventurers mentions a farmer along the *King’s Road*, telling of a large, slithering creature. The party rests before heading out in the morning.

On the *King’s Road*, they find large oily trails mixed with soot, and soon meet the farmer, who confirms that locals fear a "Grease Dragon" has taken over a shrine deep in the marsh, active just a decade ago. He also mentions his friend, Ted, saw toad-like creatures nearby. The party pays him 2 SP to watch their horses and cart before heading into the marsh on foot.

Ulrich tests the blackened grease, igniting it \- it bursts into flames instantly, proving it is highly flammable. After a day’s travel east through the marsh, they reach massive sandstone cliffs at sundown, spotting two entrances: a large open archway where oil trails converge, and a collapsed iron gate. Choosing the less obvious route, they squeeze through the rubble-filled gate, where Barny prods a rotting corpse, triggering intricate brass automaton hands to attack. The party renders them inert, and Arden pockets them, also finding three golden gears and a strange brass crank box.

Inside, they reach a chapel-like chamber with a 12ft brass statue of a serpent-headed, six-armed figure shackled by chains, gripping 3 brass lightning bolts. A rancid water basin sits before it, and a nearby mural depicts gnomes battling the same figure, now clearly a demon. Arden spots thick cobwebs, and Grog’s lantern reveals two crab spiders, which drop onto them both before being swiftly slain. As Virien searches unsuccessfully for secret doors, Ulrich finds a large spike on the statue’s back \- pulling it, he unlocks a hidden passage, though Virien believes he found it himself.

Through the secret passage, they find a locked door, which frustrates them, and a small room with rotting sofas, where they recover an accordion, bolts, and rations. Virien tests the brass box, cranking it until a small voice shouts, "For Mulvis\!". Pressing the red button, the box clicks ominously, causing the Bonebreakers to panic, fearing an explosion \- until Virien presses it again, revealing it as a recording device.

At a dead end, Virien again fails to find a hidden door, but Ulrich presses the wall, revealing a massive foundry. The now-solidified pool of iron in the forge is surrounded by five anvils, bellows, and workbenches covered in brass automaton parts and tools, with a mural showing gnome smiths commanding the demon, Mulvis, to hurl lightning at the forge. Virien searches the workbenches, finding a gold ingot, spears, a crystal bell, and a tuba. Meanwhile, Arden cautiously tries to pull out an ornate sword embedded in the solid iron pool, but it refuses to budge.

Before they can investigate further, four hunched, flabby, toad-headed humanoids \- Gloops \- enter the foundry. They ignore the Bonebreakers at first, following the oil slick as if drawn to it. Arden asks where they are going. The Gloops, seemingly entranced, say they have paid a great sum for a pilgrimage to the great serpent, who will grant their greatest desires. When pressed further, they confirm that travelers have been taken to feed the creature.

As a tense silence falls over the room, the session ends.

## Session 5 \- Shrine of the Oozing Serpent

The session starts as the four gloop pilgrims disappear to the south. As the Bonebreakers prepare to move on, Ulrich gathers tools, Arden creates a break in the grease, and Virien and Barny test the bellows, finding they work as expected. Doubling back, Ulrich dismantles the locked door, with Virien and Barny retrieving two brass lightning bolts from the statue. Behind the door, they find rotten shelves filled with moldy robes and automaton parts, along with a 6ft automaton version of the demon Mulvis, its six arms wielding shortswords. Cautiously inspecting, Arden notices a hole in its back, perfectly shaped for one of the lightning bolts.

Returning to the foundry, the party hears a cry for help from a nearby storeroom. Inside, four gloop guards are throwing darts at Eric, a captured cleric. Arden tries to bluff the gloops into handing Eric over, and the gloops reveal the creature they serve is Sootmurk, a female Grease Dragon, and their commander is Captain Gullian. Right on cue, Sootmurk’s rumbling is heard through the shrine walls, and the gloops, now convinced, march Eric into the foundry. The Bonebreakers ambush them, killing all but one gloop, whom they shackle and interrogate while Barny throws darts at it. The gloop reveals that Sootmurk has grown hungrier, forcing them to capture even more travelers.

After gagging the prisoner, the party turns to Eric, who introduces himself as a lone adventurer seeking treasure. He joins the group, and they head back to the forge, where Arden hurls a lightning bolt into the foundry, activating it into a real lightning bolt that liquefies the pool of iron. Virien cools the pool with the bellows, and Arden barely catches the ornate sword within. Virien takes the new sword, passing his \+1 sword to Grog. Just then, a pack of giant soot snails passes harmlessly through the foundry, and the group presses south of the storeroom.

They find a room filled with gnomish workbenches used for embalming, the air thick with the scent of oils. On one bench lies a sleeping gloop, which the party ties up. Moments later, two crab spiders drop onto the gloop and Ulrich, killing the gloop, but the Bonebreakers kill the spiders before more damage is done. Virien opens a door scrawled with “gnome evil ghost keep out.” Inside is a cold, misty corridor, and at a crossroad, a small automaton insect emitting a blue light floats past harmlessly.

The party discovers iron caskets lining the walls, each marked with gnomish text, but without a thief, they cannot open them. Ulrich tests every door as they go, just to make sure they are *really* locked. After finding one large casket, the group tries to catch the flying automaton, failing repeatedly, ultimately abandoning the effort. Leaving the crypt, they return to the main corridor, where they spot three gloop pilgrims covering themselves in grease to the south and four guards blocking a dozen pilgrims to the north, demanding tribute.

Arden pretends to be a ghost, frightening the southern gloops, but the northern guards remain unconvinced. Virien offers gold as tribute, then triggers chaos by pretending he’ll pay for everyone. The pilgrims scatter in confusion, and the Bonebreakers set the hall aflame, forcing everyone to flee. Amid the chaos, the party quickly loots 24 GP and 46 SP before pushing through the double doors to the south.

They enter a massive cavern, at least 50 feet high and wide, where they find Sootmurk, the serpentine Grease Dragon, surrounded by 11 gloop guards. Gullian, the gloop captain, stands before them as the shock sets in. The session ends just as the party begins to hurl a lightning bolt toward Sootmurk and the surrounding grease. This is a trial by fire.

## Session 6 \- The Dragon's Deception

As the Bonebreakers enter Sootmurk’s lair, the Grease Dragon growls, calling them fools. Without hesitation, Barny hurls a lightning bolt, striking Sootmurk and setting her ablaze. The party quickly seals the doors behind them and sets the corridor alight to block pursuit—but not before Sootmurk casts Sleep, felling the entire group.

Over an hour later, they awaken shackled in the storeroom, surrounded by 11 gloop guards. Captain Gulian begins interrogating them, and Eric bluffs that they are emissaries of a mighty Gold Dragon named Goldmark, sent to test Sootmurk’s worth. Virien doubles down, claiming they brought a gold bar as tribute, directing Gulian to his pack—who blows the Alphorn dramatically in the process. As if on cue, a deep rumbling voice echoes through the dungeon. Arden adds that Gulian could wield similar magic, like the lightning bolt, if they are freed.

Gulian, intrigued, sends his devout guards away and offers to free the party in exchange for an escort to Goldmark. The party agrees. Still disarmed, they are marched toward the entrance—where Virien and Arden stage a fake argument. Amid the distraction, Arden lights the grease trail, killing several guards and sending the rest fleeing. Captain Gulian is incinerated, while two gloops escape with the party’s weapons.

Ulrich slays one, and Barny pursues the other, eventually bringing it down with Arden’s help, who casts his last spell to save his friend. Rearmed, the Bonebreakers return through the hidden entrance to the shrine. They purify the basin’s water, refill their flasks, and retrieve the last lightning bolt.

In the chamber with the automaton, they meet Gorfthistle, a treasure-hungry gnome, and his automaton dog, Butch. Gorfthistle eyes Virien’s sword, claiming it might be linked to the treasure of King Bomfluke. Though he doesn’t know its location, the Bonebreakers do—and offer to help find it if he assists in defeating Sootmurk. He agrees.

Arden experiments with the automaton Mulvis, activating it briefly—only barely escaping death as its six blades whirl violently. They return to the foundry, fight off two crab spiders, and load the now-inert automaton onto a dolly, wheeling it back to Sootmurk’s chamber.  
![][image2]  
They burst in, catching Sootmurk and her five remaining guards off guard. Bran and Eric charge in, pushing Auto-Mulvis to deliver brutal blows to the wounded dragon. The rest of the party follows, and Sootmurk is swiftly slain. The remaining gloops, enraged, retaliate—Barny is tragically killed, but the Bonebreakers defeat them.

They discover a hoard of treasure—over 9,000 gold pieces, though they can only carry 3,200, plus a haul of gems. Arden, continuing the Goldmark deception, intimidates a surviving gloop into promising never to harm travelers again. Convinced, the gloop follows them, believing they will lead him to the Gold Dragon.

Hauling their loot and fallen comrade, the Bonebreakers cross the marsh, retrieve their cart from the farmer, and return to Barrow Spa. Ever cautious, they camp outside overnight with their treasure, then deposit it safely the next morning. Their first stop: The Last Chance, to resurrect Barny.

## Session 7 \- The Price of Greed

Back in Barrow Spa, Barny is resurrected, though he suffers from resurrection sickness and remains bedridden for a time. He uses the opportunity to study and learn new spells. Meanwhile, the Bonebreakers do some shopping, reconnect with Dreg, and hire a new thief—Neem, a shady, quiet man. After picking up their draft horse Sirius and their newly painted cart, they part ways with Eric and return to the shrine, where Gorfthistle is waiting.

In the catacombs, the group hears ghostly singing, which Gorfthistle translates as “Those who generously give, Mulvis protects.” Ignoring the warning, the party’s thieves begin meticulously opening the iron caskets, triggering traps that release paralysing gas. Both Neem and Gorfthistle are affected, but Arden cures Neem with a spell.

While this unfolds, Arden continues his comical attempts to catch the flying automaton bug, finally netting it but failing to secure it. He passes it to Bran, who loses patience and smashes it against a wall, causing it to explode, injuring Bran, Arden, and Gorfthistle. Among the opened caskets, they find a writing implement, purple ink well, and a blue robe.

Eventually, the group leads Gorfthistle to the ornate casket of King Bomfluke. Gorfthistle deftly opens it and greedily snatches the crown, while Arden quietly pockets a red dagger with a beady moving eye, along with 100GP. Spotting something odd about the casket’s backing, Arden pokes through and uncovers a hidden corridor.

Just as the group is preparing to continue, Neem backstabs Gorfthistle under cover of mist, attempting to steal the crown. Then, Neem shouts out, pretending he was the one attacked, tricking the group into thinking he’s the victim. As Virien and Arden rush to intervene, Gorfthistle—furious—executes Neem with a crossbow bolt.

The Bonebreakers (excluding Ulrich) are outraged and turn on Gorfthistle, killing him. They discover he had lied about having gold to pay them, and Arden claims the crown. With nothing else in the catacombs, they take the secret corridor, which leads into Sootmurk’s lair, only to realise it’s a one-way exit, trapping them.

As Virien works on reopening the way out, Arden tries to pry the head off Auto-Mulvis. Failing, he gives the task to Bran, who uses a magic sword to cleave it off—but the automaton explodes. Virien is safely out of range, Ulrich dives clear, but Bran, Arden, and Dreg are caught in the blast. Bran and Arden barely survive, but Dreg is killed.

Tired and bloodied, the Bonebreakers gather their loot, exit the shrine, and make the long trek back through the marsh. Once in Barrow Spa, they camp outside one more night to protect their haul, then safely deposit their treasure the next morning.

## Session 8 \- The Jeweller’s Sanctum

After their harrowing return from the shrine, the Bonebreakers spend two weeks resting in Barrow Spa. Barny recovers from resurrection sickness, using his time to study new spells. The group upgrades their gear, decorates their second wagon and horses, and Arden begins spreading the word of Belenus, handing out 1GP daily to the town’s needy.

They visit the absent-minded wizard Aldrich, who identifies several magic items:

* The Red Seer’s Dagger: lets the user see through a creature’s eyes while the dagger is stabbed in the creature.  
* The Sword of Mulvis: a blade carved from the demon’s spine, potent against fiends.  
* A Potion of Plant Control: which Aldric demonstrates by causing a Venus flytrap to dance.  
* The Crown of King Bomfluke: impervious to damage and granting the wearer immunity to poison, demonstrated by Aldrich with reckless flair.

Soon after, the party is summoned by Reginald at the *Guildhall*. He sends them to a new patron: Jessum Tarantella, the last heir of a once-great family, who seeks help restoring his manor, plagued by strange noises, shrieks, and humming. Townsfolk tell tales of Draxas Tarantella, Jessum’s grandfather, a famed jeweller and magician who built the manor and left behind vast, trap-ridden treasure. Jessum's father, however, squandered the family fortune.

The Bonebreakers travel to *Tarantella Manor*, a crumbling estate adorned with checkered stonework and spider motifs, including a large carved spider above the door. Jessum greets them humbly, even tending their horses. He leads them inside and shares his story: the noises come from Draxas’s workshop below, filled with treasure and deadly traps. A dwarf Jessum hired to explore it was heard screaming within the hour. He offers the party whatever treasure they can retrieve.

They descend into the *Jeweller’s Sanctum*, a winding limestone dungeon. At the bottom of the stairs, Jessum locks the door behind them, agreeing to open it again at the signal “Shave and a Haircut.” The air is dank, littered with cobwebs, giant rat droppings, and footprints.  
**![][image3]**

Deeper in, they pass three sets of wall-mounted faces—two black pairs and one white—and soon encounter a black-and-white checkered floor, flanked by blood-streaked slits in the wall. Ulrich tests the trap, triggering blades from the walls when he steps on a white square. He disables the trap with iron spikes, and the group discovers the safe path is all black tiles.

As they crawl through, manic laughter echoes down the hall. Following scratching sounds, they break into a side room filled with giant rats, quickly dispatching them. Barny embeds the Red Seer’s Dagger into one rat, peering through its eyes as it escapes into a tunnel. Through the rat’s vision, he sees a branching passage and a rat queen in a parlor, though he cannot understand her speech.

Among the rat nest, the party finds a spellbook, Morlan’s Marvelous Magic, containing the Sleep and Light spells. Pressing onward, they encounter a second checkered floor trap, marking the start of more dangers to come. 

## Session 9 \- Tarantella's Tune

Continuing their exploration of *The Jeweller’s Sanctum*, the Bonebreakers come across a second checkered floor trap, where a charred rat lies motionless. Suspecting a different mechanism, they intentionally trigger it, confirming it delivers a jolt of electricity when the wrong tiles are pressed. Carefully stepping only on the black tiles, which they deduce correspond to the carved black faces seen earlier, the party safely crosses.

Beyond the trap lies a large open chamber to the right. Bran peeks in, noticing shelves and movement but no detail. After a short rest, Barny uses a mirror to spot four giant centipedes feasting on books and scrolls. The party charges in—Ulrich and Bran slay one each, and Rhian and Grog finally prove themselves, finishing the rest.

The room is a long-disused library, with bookcases, an ornate spider-themed desk and chair, and a door to the west. While Barny pores over books—mostly on spiders and traps—he finds one describing mechanisms they've encountered, and hints at a summonable guardian and methods for trapping water. Soon, four more centipedes appear, and the party dispatches them swiftly.

Arden notes the desk and chair may be valuable, while Ulrich inspects the bookcases, finding one with hinges. True to form, he begins dismantling it before realizing it simply opens, revealing a narrow passage.

Bran and Arden lead the way, entering a glowing chamber with four silver statues of women playing flutes in the corners, and three spike pits open in the floor. From the ceiling descends a massive spider with a silver collar, humming a Tarantella tune. As it turns toward them, Ulrich whistles back, briefly distracting it while Arden locates a button on one statue.

Just then, two centipedes emerge, and the spider turns aggressive. As the party engages, four more centipedes burst from the walls, surrounding them. In a critical moment, Barny casts Sleep, neutralizing most of the insects, and the party quickly brings down the spider—thankfully avoiding its venomous bite.

Bran and Grog dispatch the remaining centipedes, and Barny claims the silver collar. But the respite is short—six more centipedes erupt, biting Ulrich (immune), Barny, and Rhian, before being defeated. Weakened and with two members out of action, the Bonebreakers loot what they can, using a grappling hook to lift a skeleton from a pit—gaining little.

With their resources depleted, they retreat to the entrance, hauling the silver statues with them. Jessum is delighted with their progress and eagerly awaits their return once they’ve recovered and regrouped.

## Session 10 \- Pentagrams and Pitfalls

After returning to Barrow Spa, the Bonebreakers visit Judas at *The Second Chance*, where Barny negotiates a one-time payment of 200GP per person for cure poison spells. Virien and Barny are cured, while Rhian is left to recover in bed.

After resting at the *Red Herring*, the party visits the *Bean Counter*, selling their silver statues to Ruby Sunbeam, who rewards them with free coffee. They then resupply, and Barny hires a new thief, Elon, narrowly salvaging the negotiation by calling it a "wizard’s jest."

With new retainer in tow, the party returns to Tarantella Manor. Jessum is surprised to see them back so soon but gladly lets them in. They descend once again into the Jeweller’s Sanctum.

The Bonebreakers head toward the room where they fought the large spider, entering an adjacent forge chamber decorated with murals of fiery efreet forging items. On a workbench, they find a crucible, two gemmed rings, and several ingots—silver, gold, and platinum—which Arden, Ulrich, and Virien quickly claim. Ulrich notes the hammer-and-tong imagery in the mural but finds no hidden mechanisms.

Continuing into a room south of the spider’s chamber, they discover murals of jewels infused with elemental power, a pentagram inlaid in the floor, and a desk holding a ruby ring, a large tome, and a sealed envelope. Two muscular statues wielding greatswords guard the room and demand a seal of approval. Attempts to trick them fail, and the statues advance.

Retreating into the spike-pit room, the Bonebreakers bait the statues onto the traps. Barny turns invisible, shoving one statue into a pit, while Bran dodges swinging blades and topples the other. Victorious, the party investigates the chamber.

Barny skims the genie-skin tome, finding magical research. Virien pockets the sealed envelope marked "for my grandson, Jessum." Arden tests the ruby ring, feeling immune to fire. Barny also spies through the Seer's Dagger, seeing his rat companion in a laboratory strewn with dead rats.

The Bonebreakers continue southwest, finding a workshop mural of Zorns unearthing crystals, a granite workbench, and a loom. Suddenly, seven giant centipedes attack. Grog is poisoned, but a quick Sleep spell from Barny helps the party dispatch them. More rats appear and are quickly slaughtered as Barny reclaims the Seer's dagger. Among the debris, they find 37 uncut gems and a key.

Backtracking, they puzzle over the elemental murals before heading west of the spider room. In a northern chamber, they find piles of corroded scrap metal and a locked iron casket chained inside a circle of glowing purple salt. Virien steps inside, noting that the magic in his items seems suppressed—an anti-magic field. Using the key, he unlocks the casket, finding five mysterious rings and a note reading: "Morlan, hands off\!"

Barny bravely dons a ring, only for it to curse him, reducing his armor class.  
The Bonebreakers, battered but enriched, press on, deeper into the dangerous sanctum.

## Session 11 \- The Price of Curiosity

The Bonebreakers press deeper into the *Jeweller’s Sanctum*, heading west through a corridor and discovering a northern room—a richly decorated study. Inside, they find a spider-themed desk, an embroidered chair, astrological diagrams, and a lectern holding a large checkered tome. Barny finds a boneflute on the desk and plays it, but nothing happens. The party speculates it may have once interacted with the statues or spider. Arden dons a purple glove from the desk and opens the tome, but can’t read it; Barny skims it, identifying it as a book on traps.

Continuing, the corridor ends in a southern door, which Bran breaks down. Beyond lies a large, still body of water, described in the trap book. At its bottom is the dead dwarf adventurer, his armor corroded and flesh pockmarked. Footprints indicate someone crossed—a vindication for Ulrich, who had suspected a trap here.

Virien attempts to build a raft using the broken door and pushes it into the liquid—but a grey ooze emerges, climbing his arm and dragging him into the water. His armor melts, and Virien dies a gruesome death. After several frantic attempts, Elon manages to retrieve his body. Wounded and demoralized, the group retreats.

On their way out, they’re ambushed by centipedes and rats. The entire group is poisoned except for Bran, who heroically cuts through the attackers and clears the way. Back in Barrow Spa, the party trades the sealed letter addressed to Jessum for exclusive access to the Sanctum. Jessum agrees, and Virien is resurrected. The group takes two weeks to rest and recover.

During downtime, they sell treasure and consult Aldrich, who identifies the cursed rings from the casket:

Gold: –2 AC

Silver: –2 saving throws, bad luck

Bronze: Causes nightmares, slows recovery

Lead: Prevents magic item use

Brass: –2 to attacks in daylight

After resting, the Bonebreakers return to the manor. Jessum, now sleeping “better,” gifts them a gnomish encoded tome describing local legends and phenomena.

Back in the Sanctum, they successfully navigate the third checkerboard trap by stepping only on white tiles. Exploring a southern chamber, they discover cages of all shapes, filled with the skeletons of exotic and monstrous creatures—sturges, owlbear cubs, two-headed snakes, and a zorn. One cage contains a large mirror.

Arden cautiously approaches, using a hand mirror to look into it. Reflected back is a mad, red-haired wizard in opulent garb, who introduces himself as Morlan, once Draxas’s assistant, now trapped in the mirror. He claims he made a mistake long ago, though the party suspects he's downplaying it.

Arden smashes the mirror, freeing Morlan, but only into the confines of the cage. Barny attempts to charm him magically, but fails—prompting Morlan to hurl a knife at him as the session ends in tension.

## Session 12 \- A Queen’s Death

Morlan, now free but caged, realises he’s trapped and surrenders. Seeing an opportunity, Arden trades him the cursed lead ring (unbeknownst to Morlan) in exchange for his fine amulet, then unlocks the cage. Morlan, eager for treasure, temporarily joins the Bonebreakers.

Heading west, the party enters the dusty parlor previously seen through the Seer’s Dagger—home to the self-styled Rat Queen, a giant rat wearing a magical ring, flanked by five rat guards. She demands tribute before allowing negotiation. Arden offers cursed rings, hoping to trade, but Barny, fed up, begins casting Sleep.

The rats swarm, some succumbing to the spell, while others attack. More rats appear from behind. Arden duels the Queen, Grog and Ulrich hold the rear, and Bran and Barny mow down the rest. Eventually, Arden delivers a blow to the Rat Queen’s head, killing her. The party claims a large golden bowl, which Morlan (wrongly) believes is his, and they make him carry it.

Barny dons the Queen’s ring, only to be cursed again, this time gaining the limited intellect of a very smart rat—clearly a ring meant to elevate a rat, not a human.

Returning to the acid pool trap, the Bonebreakers douse it in oil and light it, destroying the grey oozes. Just then, mourning rats ambush them, enraged by the Queen’s death. Morlan is slain, and Grog is injured but holds firm, helping the party prevail.

They explore the final room—a ruined laboratory, reeking of chemicals. Inside are shelves of multi-coloured magical powders, and a purple robe matching Arden’s glove. Arden attempts to snag the robe with a grappling hook but triggers Yellow Mould, which the party safely disperses at range. Arden dons the robe, and the group carefully bottles the powders.

With no secret doors found after a final sweep, the Bonebreakers gather their loot and expensive furnishings and exit the Sanctum. Jessum meets them at the surface, thanks them warmly, and even trades his magic ring for a handful of gems.

Back in Barrow Spa, they cash in their haul, begin decoding the gnomish tome, and discover a map hidden within its pages—showing a golden Asclepieion on an island, with a lake marked with an X, hinting at new adventure ahead.

## Session 13 \- Road to Ikiria

The Bonebreakers begin investigating the map they found in Jessum’s tome, searching for any clues about the mysterious island and the *Golden Asclepieion*. During this time, they recruit two new members to their ranks: Frank, a cunning thief, and Ehecat, a stoic and battle-hardened fighter.

As they gather context, they piece together the broader geography:

* Barrowshire lies in the western Southlands, part of East Agria.  
* To the northeast are the Northlands, and to the west, the West Marches.  
* The nearest major port is Ikiria, far to the east, perched atop seaside cliffs.

Looking to prepare, the Bonebreakers visit *The Steamy Smithy*, hoping to stock up and glean more from travelers. There, they encounter two suspicious hooded figures in the changing rooms who respond coldly to Barny’s attempts at conversation. Moments later, screams ring out from the spa.

Rushing in, the party sees the hooded pair attacking two guests—wererats in disguise. The Bonebreakers spring into action, killing one and capturing the other, though one patron is gravely wounded. Arden heals the man, crediting Belenus. Grateful, the man introduces himself as James, a coffee merchant en route to Ikiria, and offers the party advice and a future meeting.

From James, they learn:

* The journey to Ikiria is treacherous.  
* The city was built by elves, later abandoned, then renovated by gnomes.  
* It sits atop towering cliffs, with a high-tech upper district and bustling docks below.

Interrogating the captured wererat, the party learns he came from the Badlands far to the south, driven by hunger for human flesh. Barny charms him magically, and the rat—now dubbed Rattius—becomes his devoted follower for a month.

With supplies gathered, the party departs east along the river.

* Day one is calm, though they spot a strange cathedral surrounded by barren land in the distance. They choose not to investigate.  
* On night two, they're ambushed by glowing beetles. Barny casts Sleep, neutralizing them, and the party bottles their luminous cores.

On the third day, they reach the majestic city of *Ikiria*, built atop sea cliffs, its waterfall cascading into a thriving lower port. Open plazas, soaring gnomish towers, and countless ships paint a picture of bustling prosperity.

They pass through the upper city, noting its refinement, and make for the *Flux Academy*, a renowned university. A friendly gnomish porter arranges meetings for the following day:

* Ulna Glitterpatch, Head of the College of Health.  
* Herbert Newell, Master Alchemist of the College of Invention.

That evening, the Bonebreakers head to the docks to ask around for James, then settle for the night at a fine inn near the upper district: The Upper Class.

## Session 14 \- Voyage to Fos Imeras

The next morning, the Bonebreakers meet Professor Ulna Glitterpatch at the *Flux Academy*. Friendly and practical, she surprises the group by not being a magic user—her expertise lies in physical healing. Shown the mysterious map, she recognises the island as *Fos Imeras*, once a famed place of miraculous healing. Pilgrims from all over once travelled there, but no one has come or gone in some time.

Concerned, Glitterpatch offers the party 5000 GP if they can uncover what has happened on the island, covering travel and operational expenses. The Bonebreakers accept. She gives them coordinates and a formal letter, and they make their way to Ikiria’s docks to find a ship.

There, in a busy tavern, they meet Captain Nelson and his navigator, Winston, veterans of the coffee trade. Nelson agrees to take them aboard but warns of dangerous waters—bad weather, pirates, and rising aggression from the Ramen Empire, a military force once expelled from Agria. The crew begins preparation.

Next, the party visits Herbert Newell, the grumpy master alchemist of the Academy. He identifies three potions: healing, speed, and poison. Meanwhile, Barny brews five more potions of healing.

With preparations complete, the Bonebreakers board Nelson’s ship and begin their sea voyage east. As they leave, they marvel at *Ikiria’s* magic-tech marvels—floating cargo, massive lifts, and automata guards. They note the city’s militant optimism and speculate on its oligarchic government.

During the voyage, Arden blesses a sailor each day, handing out gold in the name of Belenus, and receives a divine sign—he must go to “the temple.” Frank learns to sail and plants the idea in Arden’s head that the temple may be tied to Belenus. Ulrich suffers through crippling seasickness, and Virien begins practicing the bone flute found in the Jeweller's Sanctum.

Trouble brews when pirates are spotted. Thinking fast, the Bonebreakers pretend to be plague victims suffering from Lupus, en route to Fos Imeras for healing. The pirates, disgusted, leave them in peace. Later, a golden dragon is seen soaring above the sea. Tense and in awe, the crew watches as it observes them silently before vanishing.

As they near Fos Imeras, three Ramen Empire ships surround them. A captain boards and issues the party a conditional visa—they are permitted to land if they agree to gather intelligence. They must: Investigate the disappearance of Callea, discover the fate of Ossilicus, a legendary Ramen Imperial, and recover his magical vessel, the Eleftheria. With no choice, the Bonebreakers agree.

Approaching the island, they choose the southern beach, where figures appear to be sunbathing. Disembarking, they find pale, blistered figures in tattered gray robes, attended by four in white uniforms—likely physicians and patients.

Overseeing them is a grotesque being with the body of an eagle and upper half of an old woman—a harpy, crooning eerily. As Virien approaches, her song charms him immediately. The others plug their ears with wax and attack, swiftly killing the harpy and breaking her hold over Virien. The beach secured, the party stands on the mysterious and seemingly broken island of healing, unsure what awaits them next.

## Session 15 \- The Golden Asclepion

The Bonebreakers, now on *Fos Imeras*, are joined by two new companions: Durandal, a devout cleric, and Luthien, a mysterious elven wanderer. They venture into the golden temple inland, finding it infested with harpies.

During the assault, the group manages to rescue several captives, but are forced into a hasty retreat as the creatures overwhelm them.

Disaster strikes during their escape—a violent storm shatters their ship upon the rocks. Both carts, the beloved Alphorn, and Sirius the horse are lost. The wreckage, now scattered on the bottom of the ocean, bears the nameplate of the Bonebreakers, left behind as a grim marker.

Throughout the ordeal, Arden remains distant, entranced by divine visions from Belenus. He receives a calling: to build a temple, and to heal the suffering in great numbers—his path now illuminated with sacred purpose.

## Session 16 \- Sebastaeia

The session begins in the grand hall of the *Asclepieion*, moments after the party’s tense audience with the oracle Sebastaeia. Though passive and unharmed by their earlier attacks—thanks to her precognitive abilities—Sebastaeia remains resolute in her mission: to “heal” all within the temple through a disturbing process of purification.

With them are several rescued allies: Timo the gnome thief, Cleostratus the wrestler, a musician, and a sailor. Durandal pleads with Sebastaeia to end the purification, but she refuses. In desperation, she attacks.

Sebastaeia commands her lion companion to flee and call for reinforcements. As its mighty roar echoes through the temple, the Bonebreakers know the harpies will soon come. Barny casts *Hold Portal* to seal off one entrance, successfully delaying the flood of enemies, while Arden blesses the group.

Combat begins. The lion is slain, and harpies arrive in waves. Multiple party members are charmed, but by different harpies, causing confusion without complete loss of control. Bran cuts down swaths of enemies, and eventually lands the killing blow on Sebastaeia.

In the chest near her throne, the party recovers 6 ancient pottery shards, a crystal ball, a map of the temple, and 2000 GP. As they retreat, they pass a statue and hear wet footsteps—a faceless creature glides past them, oblivious.

Continuing northeast, they come across a horrifying sight: a floating ball of flesh, made of “purified” ones, into which others are desperately crawling. Several party members enter the room and are assaulted by intense psychic ringing and nosebleeds. The group slay the attacking purified, but 16 physicians, freed from the held door, are now closing in.

Fleeing, the party attempts to use a trapdoor marked on the map—but it contains more purified. They slam it shut and escape via a secret door, finding a room filled with sick sailors.

After a short pause, they press on to the treasure room, grabbing 1600 GP, and make for the exit. In a gymnasium-like chamber, the wrestler recognises a man with black hair—it's Ossilicus, the legendary Imperial. The party reminds him of his identity, and together they escape the temple.

Outside, the group finds their cached treasure intact, sets up camp, and recovers.

The next morning, they head to the mysterious lake marked on the map. Arden drinks from its clear waters, and a beautiful figure emerges. Frank calls out, declaring the temple cleared.

The figure sings—charming some of the party. Arden and others begin stripping off armor and wading in. Virien casts *Sleep*, felling several of the blue-skinned creatures, but more keep coming.

Thinking quickly, Athlestan recalls a riddle from the temple: *a villain’s rib, a pound of gold, something purple, something old*. Producing the needed items, he throws them into the lake. A surge of magic reveals Ossilicus’ legendary ship, the *Eleftheria*.

The figures retreat, and the party boards the ship, now safe. Bran tosses his rainbow stone into the lake, revealing a vast submerged city below. The figures rise once more—Nixies, now revealed as friendly—inviting one party member down.

Frank, still charmed, descends and finds 10,000 silver pieces and a magic sword. The session ends with Frank trying to persuade the others to join him underwater.

## Session 17 \- Beneath the Surface, Above Suspicion

Still aboard the magical ship, the *Eleftheria*, the party find themselves at odds with the Nixies, who—despite their friendly demeanor—clearly intend for the party to remain in their underwater city forever. The charm magic they use, though subtle, reveals an unsettling truth: their hospitality is not optional.

Desperate to escape without violence, the party strike a bargain, promising to return with physicians from the temple to take their place. The Nixies accept this deal, allowing the party to claim the treasure: 10,000 silver pieces and a magic sword.

Upon claiming the blade, Ehecat discovers its true nature—it is sentient, a relic crafted by a druid of his own tribe, the Cassets. It urges him toward vengeance against the Ramen Empire, which slaughtered his people. Ehecat keeps this revelation to himself for now.

With the Eleftheria under their control, the group return to the *Asclepieion*, clearing the last remaining harpies from the temple. Along the way, they rescue a noblewoman, revealed to be a princess of Agria, and seven other Agrian nobles, all of whom had been captured or sedated within the temple complex.

With the temple cleared, the group escapes aboard the *Eleftheria*, learning more about its strange, modular nature—it can be assembled and disassembled using its components, allowing for swift concealment or transport.

As they sail westward, they are once more intercepted by ships of the Ramen Navy. This time, however, they are not hostile. With Ossilicus, the musician, and an imperial sailor returning to their ranks, the Ramen accept the group’s return in good faith. In a surprising twist, the navy offers to escort the Bonebreakers back to Ikiria in gratitude, their presence now legitimized by the return of the missing figures.

## Session 18 \- New Beginnings

The party returns to *Ikiria* under cover of night, unannounced and uncelebrated. Captain Nelson docks quietly, and the rescued nobles and Princess hastily thank the party—now going by no name—and disappear into the city, promising to be in touch.

Leaving the *Eleftheria* in the captain’s care, the group returns to *The Upper Class* inn in the upper city for a night of rest and reflection. There, each adventurer shares their goals and backstories:

* **Arden Sable**, a stocky man in his late 20s, was orphaned by the undead and raised by a wandering cleric whose greed shaped his worldview. A devout follower of Belenus, he dreams of elevating Belenism to the dominant religion of Agria—by royal decree. He envisions a kingdom where healing is funded through subscription tithes, undead are actively hunted, and relics are seized for the faith. His first steps: build a temple, *The Mercy*, and find its champion, *Mercy’s Blade*.  
* **Francis**, a wiry man in his early 30s, was born to a brothel worker and never knew his father. When his mother was taken by a noble, he was left to survive on the streets, learning every trick in the book. The party changed his life—money, status, and recognition are finally within reach. Meeting the princess clarified his ambitions: marry into nobility, gain influence, and become the shadow-broker of the elite—the one nobles turn to when they need something done.  
* **Ulrich**, a lean cleric with no named god, has wandered from temple to temple, receiving divine magic despite pledging to none. He seeks the “one true god,” and along the way hopes to grow strong in body, found a circle of healing clerics, and collect relics of every faith to understand their truths.  
* **Virien**, an elf from a merchant family of silks and linens, always found it dull. Reincarnated through magic after dying, he has faced death and horror—and wants more. His dream is to become a legendary hero, build a fortress, and found a mercenary company that gives others the same chance at glory.  
* **Luthien**, another elf, hated her sheltered, boring village. Never fitting in, she seeks power—and, unbeknownst to the party, mastery of dark magic. She hopes one day to convert her entire village to lawful evil, reshaping it into something worthy of her ambitions. That may just be the beginning.  
* **Barny** swore he was once *Barnobuck the Bizarre*—the most powerful wizard alive. That was before a mysterious stroke robbed him of his abilities. He blames a conspiracy of jealous mages. Barny believes he was level 100… and is now level 1\. He’s convinced he once possessed a scroll of immortality, but forgot where he put it. His goals: become immortal and recover the truth of his forgotten past.  
* **Ehecat**, the stoic fighter, comes from the Casset tribe—once proud knights and druids, now ash, destroyed by the Ramen Empire. Taught by his father, he’s a man out of place, seeking belonging. His goal is clear: dismantle the Ramen Empire, beginning with the bloodline of the officer who wiped out his people. He shares this with no one—but Bran, whose past mirrors his, nods in silent agreement.  
* **Durandale**, a travelling cleric of Lathandre, was raised among many faiths, eventually choosing the god of light. But temple life felt naive. She set out to see the world and test her ideals—though her true desire is to return home, to a dangerous land few survive reaching.  
* **Athlestan Ghoulsbane**, cleric of Coranth, drops the final revelation. He belongs to a hidden brotherhood of 100 priests, all sworn to destroy the King of Ghouls, a lich who rises every century. Each priest reincarnates with only two memories: how they last died, and their quest. They have no temple, no home, and can never meet.

The party formally divides up loot and reflects on how some of their goals align, and some may conflict. The next day, they receive a letter from the East Agria Company, summoning them to a meeting. First, they deal with business. At the *Flux Academy*, Herbert Newell identifies two potions: a potion of control Gold Dragon, and a potion of gaseous form. Professor Morrel is given the gnomish coded documents from Jessum’s book and the *Asclepieion*. Barny visits Aldrich Zaxarus, the archmage and head of the *College of Magic*—who doesn’t remember him. To learn more, Barny must enroll. Arden and Frank give out 15 GP to the poor in Belenus' name at the docks, drawing a small crowd. Frank warns the crowd off, and Arden assures Belenus' blessings will follow. Frank also begins seeking informants among noble households.

At the *East Agria Company HQ*, the group is finally ushered into a grand office and formally greeted by Princess Agatha herself—now revealed as: “Her Royal Highness, Princess Agatha, heir to the throne, Duchess of the Southlands, Mayor of Ikiria, and Governor of the East Agria Company.”

She is flanked by the newly dubbed *Admiral* Nelson and Commander Smith, her head of security. She thanks the party, acknowledges their ambitions, and proposes a deal. She will offer high-profile, secret missions. The missions are entirely optional, but must remain confidential. If betrayed, the penalty is death. The group accepts, and Ulna Glitterpatch enters, providing their 5000 GP reward for their report on Fos Imeras.

The first mission is detailed. The Deathless Plague in the Duchy of the Southlands has ravaged the region for over a decade. Victims slowly rot and eventually rise as undead. Once treated by the *Church of the Crimson Flame*, the gates now only open for the reviled Crimson Knights. The church’s behaviour is increasingly cult-like, and the afflicted are enthralled. The party’s task: end the deathless plague, by any means.

Commander Smith promises to find a survivor for questioning. The party also asks why the Princess was on *Fos Imeras*—she explains it was a covert diplomatic mission to meet the *Ramen Empire*, though a storm caused her shipwreck. She explains that *Agria* is a feudal monarchy with no standing army or navy, while Rame is a military dictatorship, causing tension. Arden casts a healing spell upon her, blessing the Princess with the light of Belenus, as Frank also praises Belenus.

The session ends as the party prepares to meet with Commander Smith the next day, where their investigation into the plague begins.

## Session 19 \- The Bell Tolls

The party transitions to the OSE Advanced Fantasy ruleset, and decides that retainers will now be employed by individual player characters rather than shared as party assets.

While having breakfast at *The Upper Class*, a hooded stranger approaches. Frank, assuming they’re a server, casually requests coffee, but is promptly ignored. The figure pulls down their hood, revealing Commander Smith in disguise. He updates the party on their mission and advises approaching the cathedral via the forest, to avoid being seen on the river route.

The Bonebreakers agree and are joined by a new member: Alinar, a magic-user. After purchasing horses, they ride north, then west, camping overnight in the woods. Nearing the *Cathedral of the Crimson Flame*, they find a large structure within a 15-foot high outer wall, surrounded by thick trees and overgrown gardens. The northern half of the building features a massive dome with smoke rising from the top; the southern half is a smaller, one-storey structure adorned with stained glass windows.

After a quiet night, the party returns at dawn, leaving their horses behind. Frank scales the outer wall, but spots three knights—one human, two undead—and quickly drops back down. The group circles around to a new vantage point, scaling the wall and entering the grounds. Frank climbs again—this time a second inner wall overlooking the central plaza, beyond the outer enclosure.

Inside, he sees trainee soldiers drilling under a gruff red-haired sergeant, beside a twisted bell mounted in a wooden frame. With Arden casting Bless, the Bonebreakers launch a surprise assault, cutting down Sergeant Grimlocke before he can shout a warning.

Ulrich tries to destroy the bell with fire, but a trainee manages to ring it before it collapses. Arden knocks out two trainees for questioning, but Bran—taking initiative a step too far—dispatches several more without pause.

The party secures the area: Ulrich and Frank spike the plaza doors, and Athlestan constructs a barricade. Timo and Alinar take cover, while Frank climbs to a high vantage point with his bow.

Soon, five Crimson Knights and a powerful Son of Bahal burst through the southern door. Attempts to turn the undead fail, and most attacks bounce off their armor.

Arden is slain, struck down while proclaiming the fury of Belenus. With his final breath, he hands Bran a note and his holy symbol. The group fights on—Alinar casts Magic Missile, Frank takes shots, and Durandale is gravely wounded.

In desperation, Timo casts Improved Phantasmal Force, crafting the illusion of a collapsing church wall. The knights hesitate, confused. Durandale sees through the illusion and bravely charges the Son of Bahal, but is tragically slain just before landing her blow.

The session ends with the illusion fully taking hold, the knights seemingly trapped beneath the illusory rubble, as the surviving Bonebreakers regroup amidst grief and smoke.

## Session 20 \- The Burned and the Bound

In a flashback, Virien visits the *White Horse Inn* in *Ikiria’s* docks to recruit new muscle. He hires the “legendary” duelist Kargor “Viperhand” for 3GP a day and a half share of treasure—plus all the ale he can drink with Virien. Selvar the Elf also joins the party.

Back in the present, Timo concentrates to maintain her illusion, keeping the first wave of Crimson Knights incapacitated. Just then, two more knights and another Son of Bahal enter. Thinking quickly, Luthien casts Web to trap them, and Athlestan silences them. They incapacitate and bind one of them for later questioning.

Athlestan then charges the undead knight, resisting its paralysing gaze again and again. Alongside Bran, he slays the Son of Bahal, and the group finishes off the rest. Among the loot: seven fine longswords, two brutal greatswords (claimed by Bran and Virien), and two twisted suits of plate armour taken by Virien and Luthien.

After the fight, Bran kills a tied-up initiate, both to test his new weapon and avenge Arden. The party moves into the southern cathedral, discovering a black-marble hall with eerie flame reflections and three unconscious prisoners chained to pillars.

After some coaxing, one prisoner reveals he was taken from a nearby village in the night. Frank frees two from their locked chains, failing on the third, and the weakened captives follow the party.

The Bonebreakers explore a corridor of stained glass and find an empty barracks with footlockers—inside, a few trinkets worth 44GP in total. Deciding not to push their luck, they collect Arden’s body, the bound knight, the unconscious initiate, and the final prisoner (freed by Virien casting knock) and head to the southern exit of the cathedral.

Two knights guard the vined, rusting iron gates, but Virien and Selvar put them to sleep with quick spellcasting. As the party exits the cathedral grounds, they overhear initiates bragging about torturing prisoners, and spot a burned corpse in a gibbet hung near the gate. Virien casts Hold Portal to seal the gate behind them.

Before they can escape, another Son of Bahal returns to the cathedral, leading two new prisoners. He attempts to paralyse Virien (to no effect), and Athlestan charges, dealing massive damage before being paralysed himself. After many misses, Selvar finishes off the undead, and the two young captives are freed.

Reaching safety, Commander Smith awaits the party. Bran immediately rides hard to *Barrow Spa*, Arden’s body in tow. Reaching *The Second Chance* in the dead of night, he finds Judas the cleric charges double for nocturnal resurrections—so he goes to sleep at *The Red Herring* instead. After a fine breakfast, Bran returns and pays Judas with Arden’s own coin, bringing him back to life. Arden gasps back to life, weakened but alive, and Bran vows to stay for a few days.

Meanwhile, the party questions the two rescued boys, who reveal they’re from a nearby farming village frequently raided by the church. The group returns them home, where Ulrich wins over their frightened father, and the party receives food and shelter for the night.

There, they interrogate the captured Crimson Knight, who refuses to speak at first, muttering that “everyone is infected.” After Luthien casts Charm Person, he reluctantly shares more. He believes only the Knights and Sons of Bahal are pure; the rest of the world is diseased and undead. The Crimson Bishop, their “source of purity,” leads the church.

When asked about the Bishop, the knight reveals he’s “everywhere,” but once saw him enter a secret door in the NW room near the northern dome. He also slips that the library in the NE near the dome is locked, containing tomes on Divine Doubt and The Dark Arts, and that one of 12 priests, and a Captain Fardr, each hold a key.

With vital information now in hand, the Bonebreakers prepare to rest and plan their return to the cathedral.

## Session 21 \- Soup for the Abbott

The Bonebreakers awoke at the farmstead to find a newcomer: Sir Cedric of House Dawnmere, a knight in fine chainmail who immediately accused Virien of being a Crimson Knight because of his armour. Frank smoothed things over, and Cedric introduced himself as the last of a minor noble house wiped out by undead. He held back details, but agreed to join the group as they prepared to return to the Cathedral.

At the rusted flame-carved gates, Virien lost patience for stealth, spurring his warhorse through and smashing them open. Frank followed dramatically by throwing wide the main doors, leading a mounted charge into the echoing hall. Finding no enemies, they spiked the doors shut and pushed west, where they found a lone knight asleep in a barracks and killed him before he stirred. Soon, two more knights returned; Ehecat, Barny, and Rattius cut down one, while Virien and Kargor felled the other. Then an undead Son of Bahal rounded the corner. Cedric nearly turned it, but failed—and the fight went poorly, with everyone missing blows before the creature paralysed Barny. Eventually, the Son was slain, and Barny freed from its gaze.

Back in the main hall, the party set a trap. When four more Sons of Bahal advanced from the courtyard, Virien, Cedric, Ehecat, and Kargor charged in on horseback. Frank tried to slip behind for a backstab but failed, and Barny hurled daggers from the rear. Two allies were paralysed while Cedric narrowly withstood the gaze and Virien was immune. Realising the odds, the group retreated—Frank whisked Ehecat away on his horse, while Barny webbed the undead and slammed the door. His crystal ball showed the area now clear.

Turning east, they found a chamber of twelve ragged priests huddled on straw. Scrawls on the walls read: *“The work of Bahal is work in blood. Death to the infected.”* Hungry and fearful, the priests handed over a key to the library in exchange for the promise of food. The party left them behind and pushed on into a filthy kitchen, where a whistling cook tended two cauldrons. Mistaking them for knights, he served gristle stew—but Barny secretly poisoned the pot, killing him on the spot. Donning knightly uniforms and pushing the bubbling cauldron, the Bonebreakers prepared their ruse: “Soup for the Abbott\!”

They bluffed their way into the northern dome, a vast nave of soot-darkened stone and crimson banners. In a side chamber, they found Captain Fardr, a once-proud officer in plate, now incoherent and muttering as he slashed at imagined foes. Frank’s pickpocket attempt failed, but Selvar charmed him into joining. Just then, four undead Sons of Bahal patrolled past. The party’s cries of “Soup for the Abbott\!” did not fool them, but Virien sealed the door with magic, and the group smashed windows to escape with Fardr.

Back at the farmstead, Fardr raved about betrayal. He revealed that the Crimson Bishop himself was no longer alive \- turned undead two years ago, now the source of corruption. Once a servant of Bahal, he had become an abomination. Fardr swore to follow Belenus if the Bonebreakers could purge the undead.

The next day, the party stormed back into the Cathedral, charging the full length of the nave on horseback and bursting through the crimson banners. At the altar they found a towering bonfire of bones, seven golden chalices stained with blood, two Sons of Bahal, and four Crimson Knights. The fight was vicious: Barny webbed a cluster of enemies, Frank tried dousing them with holy water, Fardr fought with surprising skill, Cedric struck true with steel and faith, and the others piled in until the chamber was cleared.

They then sought the Bishop’s quarters. Behind a secret door lay a spotless, richly furnished study, its four red candles flaring to life as they entered. In an instant, Virien, Cedric, Kargor, Rhian, Selvar, and even Rattius were paralysed. Ehecat and Frank barricaded the door with a bed, uncovering a hidden magical holy symbol and the diary of the *original* Bishop himself—revealing that he feared being replaced.

Invisible and impatient, Barny slipped away to the library. Inside, he found a pitch-black chamber thick with cobwebs, coins and gems glinting across the floor, and shelves of tomes: biographies, works on divine doubt, and treatises on the dark arts. Fixated, he seized a dozen books on the latter. Above him, spiders stirred.

## Session 22 \- Frank’s Gambit and the Finger of Death

Back in the Bishop’s quarters, the Bonebreakers claimed a strange translucent sword from the body of a fallen Son of Bahal, which Timo quickly took up. Re-reading the original Bishop’s diary, they uncovered a grim history: the Church’s desperate failures to purge the deathless plague, sliding from failed cures to torture and executions. The last entry, written two years prior, spoke of a necrotic presence entering the Cathedral and the Bishop preparing to face it.

While Barny scoured the library, the others shook free of paralysis and regrouped in the nave. Two faint circles marked the stone floor, and the altar showed scrape marks as if it had shifted before. When brute force failed, Timo’s sharp eyes fell on the nearby statues. Frank, in a flash of genius, yanked on their swords, and with a groan of stone the altar slid open, revealing stairs descending into darkness. From below rose a low, ghoulish chanting.

Cedric led the descent into a chamber mirroring the altar room above, this one lit by cold purple flames. At its center stood The Crimson Bishop—tall, regal, smiling faintly in his golden robes and tiara—four unconscious prisoners at his feet. He offered the party use of the Church if they pledged loyalty to him. Cedric countered, demanding instead that he cleanse the undead. The Bishop only laughed.

When Frank’s sneaking failed and Barny tried to slip away, combat broke. Athlestan blessed the group, Barny unleashed a roaring fireball that engulfed the Bishop in searing flame. Yet the figure moved with unnatural speed, dodging the worst of it, his robes smouldering but intact. Rhian hurled her dagger, only for it to clatter uselessly from his golden robes—the realization struck that he was immune to mundane weapons.

Then, with a calm, almost amused expression, the Bishop raised a single gnarled finger at Barny and uttered Finger of Death. Barny’s eyes went wide, his body went rigid, and with barely a sound he collapsed lifeless to the floor. The Bishop laughed, and then cast Fly, lifting himself effortlessly above their reach, mocking them from on high.

Cedric raised the newly found red sun holy symbol, discovering it carried power against the undead—but his turning failed. He tossed it to Athlestan, who held it for later. Meanwhile, Timo conjured an illusory holy rain with Phantasmal Force, and for a moment the Bishop’s ghoulish features flickered across his stately visage.

It was Frank who saved them. With cunning bravery, he drank his potion of gaseous form, drifted up unseen, reformed on the Bishop’s back, and grappled him—one hand clamped firmly over his mouth. He could no longer speak, no longer cast. Rattius caught the rope dangling from Frank’s belt, hauling both down in a desperate tug-of-war. Cedric seized the grapple, bracing against the Bishop’s fiery claws as Athlestan—sped by Barny’s potion of speed—became a blur of holy strikes. At last, panic entered the Bishop’s eyes. Athlestan hammered home the final blow, and with a shriek, the Bishop’s body dissolved into a noxious cloud of ashes that quickly dissipated, leaving only his precious robe and tiara behind.

The prisoners then rose, snarling, as ghouls, but Athlestan raised the holy symbol against them. Power coursed through him and the creatures shrieked, driven out into the night.

From a small iron chest in that chamber, the Bonebreakers looted richly: 1,000 gold, 3,500 silver, 35 platinum, scrolls of powerful spells, and the Bishop’s golden tiara of the Crimson Sun and necrotic robes, each worth thousands.

Exploring further west, at the end of a tunnel they found a pit of ash and half-burnt flesh, the open sky above. Frank, scouting ahead, was horrifically infested with rot grubs burrowing under his skin, toward his heart. After several frantic attempts, only fire seared them out, saving him just in time.

Deeper south, an archway led to a spiral staircase descending from the closed ceiling, then vanishing through the floor, into blackness. When Cedric dropped a torch, it seemed to fall forever, illuminating as it fell an apparently infinite staircase. A voice whispered from below: *“There’s treasure, come see…”* Uneasy, they withdrew.

Back in the library, Frank fired an arrow into the webs above, dislodging three enormous grave spiders. Webbed and bitten, he succumbed to their venom—tragically slain only hours after his heroism had saved the party from the formidable Bishop. His death struck them hard. Still, they fought on, noting how Timo’s blade drank blood from each wound it dealt. Among the bookshelves they found more treasure—gems, idols, sceptres, and the “unauthorised autobiography” of one *Baronbold the Brilliant*, within which Barny (when revived) would later find tantalising hints about a scroll of immortality.

At last, the party freed the imprisoned priests and Captain Fardr, persuading them to abandon Bahal and devote themselves to Belenus. The Cathedral was now under their control, and the deathless plague was finally lifted.

Commander Smith soon arrived, praising their grim victory despite its cost, and arranged their reward from Princess Agatha: 25,000 gold, and an official claim on the Church and its grounds.

The return to Barrow Spa brought one last grim chuckle. In the dead of night they pounded on Judas’ door at the Second Chance, only to be told resurrection cost double at that grim hour. Grumbling, they slept at the Red Herring, enjoyed a fine breakfast from Calley O’Toole, and then—at last—Barny and Frank were magically revived.

Weeks passed in recovery. Athlestan researched a spell to hunt ghouls. Rhian delved into strange plant-magic. Arden, now appointed Bishop, began training priests into clerics, and together with Athlestan, reshaped the Cathedral into a temple of Belenus and Coranth, removing its crimson flames. Barny, restless as ever, devoured the biography of Baronbold, discovering hints of a burial mound where he may have hidden his greatest treasure—perhaps even the scroll of immortality.

## Session 23 \- Secrets in the Stone

The Bonebreakers, flush with treasure, divided their spoils and rested. But Barny, restless and secretive, attempted to slip away toward the Barrow alone. Frank spotted him and raised the alarm, and the party insisted on accompanying him back into the cursed mound—whether he liked it or not.

They re-entered through the cave-side entrance, Virien and Athlestan leading the way. Strange noises echoed from the spider’s old chamber, where a baby carcass crawler lunged from the dark. The fight was chaotic—blades whiffing, venom paralysing Athlestan and Virien—until Arden’s divine magic freed Virien, and Barny’s sleep spell allowed the party to finish the beast. They waited for Athlestan to recover before pressing on.

Exploring north and east, the adventurers found a skeletal tree in a cavern, its branches scraping the stone. It creaked a greeting: *“Back to the grave, little ones.”* To their surprise, it was a treant, raised into undeath against its will. Arden explained their mission, and the treant spoke of one lone knight who had passed north before the Bonebreakers’ arrival. In a moment of mercy, Frank offered release, setting the creature alight. The flames consumed it, though Arden’s attempt to warm his hands nearly earned him the treant’s spite as it burned.

Further on, the Bonebreakers uncovered a cavern stained with blood and a blue ooze, where Ehecat recovered a blood-caked sword of no worth. Deeper still, they found a nest of bones and moss, and a talking skull claiming to be Sir Gallant, once a knight against the orcs, though his coarse manner betrayed little chivalry. Virien turned up a holy symbol amid the nest, which Ulrich claimed. At once, he heard the telepathic voice of Sir Ignacious, a righteous paladin of the “one true god,” calling him to be just and steadfast. Gallant scoffed at Ignacious’ strict code when asked, mocking him even in death.

North again, the caverns ended in a chamber with a pool of opalescent water ringed by crystal flowers. Virien boldly ate one, finding it popped like candy and healed his wounds. Selvar drank from the pool, also restored, while Arden collected a vial only to find it turned flat. Barny waded into the waters, tingling, while Ulrich cast light into the depths, seeing only pure clarity below.

But Barny had other plans. While the party investigated, he slipped away invisibly, sneaking south-east into the mossy chambers once belonging to the fairy Alfwine. There he uncovered a black stone concealing a coffer of 500 gold. When skeletons marched past, he froze until they passed, then pushed deeper into Quintius’ quarters. There, he uncovered a grimoire and a scroll, convinced this was the knowledge he had been seeking all along.

Meanwhile, the Bonebreakers thought Barny had been taken, charging back through the halls. Athlestan obliterated a band of skeletons with his new holy symbol, while Barny rejoined them feigning innocence. Together, they finally cleansed Quintius’ chamber: Arden scrubbed the circle of glyphs, releasing a wave of unseen power that scoured the Barrow of necromancy. At last, the undead threat was ended.

Barny, however, was not ready to let go. He convinced the party that the Barrow should be annexed as a place of magical research, and the other spellcasters agreed. The lair was now his domain.

The session closed with the church reorganised under the Bonebreakers’ hands: Captain Fardr overseeing the grounds, monks tending upkeep, clerics divided between Athlestan’s training, Ulrich’s research, and Bishop Arden’s tithe-gathering flock. Both the Barrow and the Cathedral now stood firmly in their grasp.

## Session 24 \- Ninjas in the Dark

The newly restored Church hums with purpose. The priests have their orders: six rebuild the halls, two train as spies under Athelstan, two as researchers under Ulrich, and two as clerics beneath Bishop Arden. Routine settles in — the doors barred each night, one priest always stationed by the courtyard bell, and the Bonebreakers rotating night watch.

A few nights in, Frank is on duty when he hears faint movement outside — first to the east, then to the west. Suspicious, he creeps to the courtyard and suddenly spots shadows vaulting the wall. He raises the alarm, shouting for the bell.

The peal rings loud — but it’s too late. Twenty-one orcs, clad in dark, silent garb, surge over the walls. One snatches the priest from the bell rope and vanishes back into the night. The rest split into two assault teams, flanking the church. Frank fires a crossbow bolt into one, then throws a net, tangling five of the intruders.

Meanwhile, in the distant Barrow, Barny’s crystal ball flickers to life. He sees the chaos at the church and immediately rallies Luthien and Selvar. In the name of Belenus, they call upon the townsfolk for aid, recruiting twenty villagers for ten gold each upfront and five more on success. Together, they set out — but they are hours away.

Back at the church, the orcs swarm through the doors. The southern team charges the priests, while in the north, Krazak the Silent, their fearsome leader, bursts into Athelstan’s chamber. Steel clashes in the dark — Athelstan barely survives the duel, gravely wounding Krazak in return.

Arden bellows a Blessing of Belenus, and the battle turns. Cedric cuts one orc down while Bran and Kargor carve through others. Frank sets his net alight, burning trapped orcs alive. Virien casts Sleep, felling another, as arrows and steel flash in the candlelight.

But the assault is not about victory — it’s a raid for hostages. Ignoring the carnage, the remaining orcs grab four priests and blow a retreating horn. Bran and Cedric slay two as they flee, but Krazak, bleeding heavily, escapes into the night. Frank manages to tackle one orc, stabbing him through the neck — but the rest vanish beyond the walls, dragging their captives away.

By dawn, the surviving villagers arrive, weary but ready for a fight. Before plans can form, an arrow thunks into the courtyard with a note tied to it. In crude but clear script, it reads:

“Bishop — I have four of your priests. They live. Bring 60,000 gold to the Kelfrek Marsh tonight. You may bring two guards. If I see soldiers, they die.  
 — Gruumsh One-tusk, Warlord of the Kelfrek Marsh.”

The Bonebreakers convene, debating desperate measures — illusionary gold, recruiting the Gloops, or storming the old Shrine of Mulvis where they once fought the Grease Dragon.

They interrogate their lone surviving orc. Suspended over the bottomless pit, he spits defiance, calling Virien a “filthy elf.” Luthien tries a different approach — first attempting to hug and kiss him into submission, which only disgusts the orc further — before finally casting Charm, forcing his obedience.

With glazed eyes, the orc yields. There are a hundred orcs, he says, hiding in the shrine, with Gruumsh himself at the head. The hostages are alive. Gruumsh, he insists, “is an orc of his word.”

To confirm, Barny peers into the crystal ball once more — the orc speaks truth. A hundred of them prowl the shrine’s halls, their foundry running, and the four priests bound where the Bonebreakers once were.

Arden decides to stall. A message by arrow is sent, and a message comes back, offering partial ransom — 15,000 gold now for one hostage, 45,000 tomorrow for the rest. The party agrees.

The next day, Arden, Bran, and Virien ride into the marsh. From the shadows of the old shrine, the massive orc warlord emerges. One terrified priest is exchanged for the gold. Arden tries to frighten Gruumsh with warnings of the shrine’s “curse”, but the warlord only grins and disappears back inside.

The Bonebreakers retreat to plan — the gold may buy time, but the rescue will demand steel, cunning, and deception.  
 The session ends as they settle on their next move: infiltration.

## Session 25 \- A Deal with Gruumsh (And Other Bad Ideas)

The Bonebreakers, weary but resolute, regroup at the Church. Captain Fardr is summoned to join them, while the remaining priests and village militia are left to fortify the grounds. With their mission clear — rescue the remaining hostages and destroy Gruumsh Onetusk’s warband — they set out once more into the wilds.

Passing through Barrow Spa, they stock up on supplies (and seven casks of wine), before trudging into the Kelfrec Marsh, its air thick with decay. Ever the pragmatist, Ulrich fills a barrel with leftover grease from the trails of the long-dead ooze, Sootmark — a decision that will soon prove invaluable.

As they near the old Shrine of Mulvis, Luthien turns to their charmed orc captive, Cronk, and releases him. “You’re no captive — we’re best friends,” she insists. The orc beams, free at last, though still under her spell. Together with Arden and Bran, she approaches the shrine’s gates, where six guards stand watch.
