Moments later, Gruumsh Onetusk himself emerges — massive, tusked, and seething with command. Luthien and Arden offer him Cronk and the wine as a supposed tribute, hoping to lull the orcs into drunken complacency. But Gruumsh refuses, demanding the deal be honoured exactly as written. Defeated, they retreat with a confused Cronk in tow.

That night, beneath the cover of mist and moonlight, the Bonebreakers put their plan into motion. They scale the cliffs to the south and slip into the shrine’s ruined southern doorway, unseen. Passing through rubble-strewn halls and the statue chamber of Mulvis, they move into the hidden rooms beyond that once held the automaton. Inside, Frank scavenges two gnomish power cores, six automaton arms, and two mechanical eyes — prizes from a bygone age.

Beyond, they hear the steady roar of the foundry. Barny, muttering under his breath, casts Invisibility on Frank, who slinks ahead to scout. What he finds chills him:

* Twenty orcs toil in the forge.  
* Krazak the Silent stands guard to the south, flanked by three messengers.  
* Six orcs guard the three captured priests in the north-east chamber.  
* Eight more sleep in the embalming room.  
* The catacombs to the west are still choked with mist.

Carefully, Frank lays tripwires every ten feet through the corridor before returning unseen to report. The Bonebreakers prepare. On the signal of thirty seconds, they move.

Frank, invisible, creeps up and deftly pickpockets Krazak’s war horn. Then, in planned unison, Barny, Selvar, and Luthien unleash a trio of Sleep spells — every orc in the foundry and prison collapses, save Krazak, one messenger, and a lone guard. Rhian seals the main door with Hold Portal, trapping any reinforcements inside.

Ulrich steps forward, raising his holy symbol — Hold Person freezes Krazak mid-breath. Bran, under the effect of a Potion of Speed, becomes a blur of steel, cleaving down the last prison guard. Arden and Rattius dispatch the messenger. In seconds, thirty orcs are dead or unconscious.

Just as they catch their breath, four orcs wander in for the change of watch — and stumble into Frank’s tripwires. Chaos erupts. Cedric slays one, Ulrich crushes another, and Luthien and Selvar cut down the rest.

Pressing on, the party storms the embalming room. The eight sleeping orcs there barely stir before Bran’s whirlwind of blades cuts through four of them, the others falling to Luthien, Selvar, Rattius, and Arden in turn.

As they regroup, the entrance guards return — only to trigger another line of tripwires and face a storm of steel. Arden, Selvar, Rhian, and Ulrich join the fray, while Bran, still alight with magical speed, cuts down two more. The last falls beneath Ulrich’s mace.

With the shrine’s northern rooms silent, the Bonebreakers unlock the prison and lead the trembling priests to safety, hiding them in the secret Mulvis chamber under Captain Fardr’s watch.

Meanwhile, Barny drags the paralysed Krazak into a side room. What happens next, only he knows — but when he returns, Krazak walks behind him, silent and stiff. The others assume he’s been charmed, unaware that Barny has sacrificed his own health to raise the orc as an undead thrall.

Now ready for their final act, the Bonebreakers douse the corridors with Ulrich’s barrel of grease. When Rhian’s Hold Portal fades, the shrine erupts with shouts — Gruumsh and eleven of his elite “ninja” orcs surge forth, blades gleaming. “Kill the spellcasters first\!” Gruumsh roars.

The Bonebreakers unleash their trap. Arrows and bolts fly — then Frank strikes a spark. The corridor ignites in a wall of flame, engulfing the charging orcs. Screams echo as several fall burning, the rest pressing on through the inferno. The heroes fall back, lighting a second trap — more grease, more fire — the shrine itself becoming a furnace of death.

When the smoke clears, Gruumsh remains, flanked by five scorched elites. The battle is brutal. Luthien and Barny are both wounded badly, but stand their ground. Gruumsh bellows orders from the rear, his voice rising over the clash of steel.

Luthien, bloodied but resolute, casts Sleep one final time — the last of the elites slump lifelessly to the ground, and the Bonebreakers descend upon them. Surrounded and outmatched, Gruumsh raises his hands in surrender.

He offers a bargain: Gronk for his treasure. Arden mocks him, laughing off the deal. Gruumsh is bound by Selvar instead, and his horde’s riches are claimed — 15,000 gold, 2,500 in stolen Church treasures, and another 4,000 in plunder.

Frank finally lets his invisibility fade. He steps up to the beaten warlord, carves a deep scar into his face, and tells him coldly to spread word of the Bonebreakers’ might. Gruumsh, seething but alive, accepts the “new deal” — his life for his gold — and disappears into the night.

The shrine burns low behind them as the Bonebreakers stand victorious once more.

## Session 26 \- The Day the Steel Spoke

With Gruumsh’s warband shattered and the Church secured, the Bonebreakers turn their gaze eastward once more. The party leaves Sir Cedric and the priests to tend the church, while they set out for Ikiria.

On arrival, Frank quickly finds opportunity in the lower docks. For 15 gold a month, he rents an empty warehouse, bare but sturdy, and immediately begins renovations. The front will serve as a Temple of Belenus — “The Temple of Merciful Life” — while the back, hidden behind crates and curtains, will double as a hub for spies, thieves, and informants. A wooden crate draped with a yellow cloth becomes the altar, a painted sun symbol above it. Yet in the back rooms lies a real shrine, with a worn prayer book — for beneath the cunning, Frank’s belief burns true.

While he decorates, Virien scours the Upper City, finding Frank an apartment fit for his growing ambitions — somewhere to host nobles and whisper deals over wine.

It’s during this time that Merrick, a flamboyant half-elf bard with wine on his breath and only three strings on his lute, waltzes into the warehouse. “Sir Francis\! I hear you’re in need of a bard.” Frank, delighted, hires him immediately — tasking him to compose a grand ballad: how Frank rescued Princess Agatha, how Virien slew thousands of harpies, how Admiral Nelson led their escape, and how they narrowly survived the gold dragon “Gozrazah” (a total fabrication). Athelstan chimes in, insisting the song mention the King of Ghouls, and the coming doom of the undead. Frank instructs Merrick to perform it in taverns — loudly — but never reveal who hired him.

Moments later, the city outside erupts in screams. Frank’s sword begins talking, whining about being replaced by a bard. Then Arden’s mace pipes up — eager to “talk about their feelings.” Athelstan’s mace nags him about his obsession with the undead. Ulrich’s weapon sighs about his lack of purpose. Barny’s dagger trembles, muttering it’s seen too much and needs to hide. Luthien’s sword demands she commit something “truly evil,” while Selvar’s crimson blade insults him for weakness against the undead.

The din spills into the streets — the entire city of Ikiria echoes with shouting steel. Exhaustion grips the Bonebreakers. Guards rush by, wrapping their weapons in cloth, shouting, “It’s him again\!”

Frank pulls one aside — the man tells him that all weapons must be taken to Professor Longtooth at the Flux Academy. Another passerby rants about years of magical disasters — melted statues, a portal to the Plane of Fire, water turning purple — before storming off, declaring he’s done with Ikiria.

As the group heads uphill toward the Upper City, Ulrich spots a distant balcony — a gnome in fine robes speaks with a hooded figure, but he can’t make out the building. Frank, meanwhile, deftly pickpockets a passing noble for 100 gold, while Arden persuades a frightened citizen to hand over their sentient weapon and visit the “temple” later for guidance.

In the Upper City, the streets gleam with order — automata patrols glide between towers. When Athelstan, baffled by their construction, tries to grapple one, the metal guard retaliates. Arden leaps in to defend him, and the pair knock it unconscious before fleeing the scene.

The citizens who have surrendered their weapons look lighter, freer — the Bonebreakers, still armed, feel the drag of weariness. Ulrich fashions a crude wooden club, finding it mercifully silent.

They visit a potioner’s shop, The Precisely Measured Scroll, run by Helvian, a sharp-eyed human woman. Frank buys a potion of lesser restoration; Athelstan purchases a map of the Tombs of Westmarch, a dangerous region west of the Southlands. Helvian reveals that Professor Screever Longtooth, though respected, is shielding a troublesome wizard — Arkeus Whizkeyrd — from disciplinary action. The council, led by Nixx Pocketbrain, head of the city’s seven merchant lords, refuses to dismiss her.

Determined to seek answers, the party heads to the East Agria Company Headquarters, hoping to meet Princess Agatha. They’re stonewalled by a bureaucratic secretary. Ulrich lingers behind and warns Commander Smith about Frank’s hired bard and the wild tale spreading through taverns. Smith’s face darkens. “I’ll handle it,” he says quietly.

Finally, the group arrives at the Flux Academy, where adventurers leave empty-handed and automata escort the uncooperative out. The porter leads them to Professor Screever Longtooth, a kind but exhausted Ratfolk scholar with spectacles and soot-streaked fur.

Inspecting their weapons, she confirms the truth — they are being drained of life by the sentience infecting their arms. Within ten hours, many in the city will fall comatose or dead. The source must be found, or Ikiria will collapse.

She believes only one man could cause this — Arkeus Whizkeyrd, her old mentor and friend. Once brilliant, now erratic, his experiments often twist the city itself. Longtooth asks for their help: find the spell component or caster responsible, and she’ll grant them access to the private faculty archives. She requests — recover a translucent tuning fork, an arcane device used in planar resonance studies. If it’s in his tower, it’s proof of his guilt.

Armed with a letter of recommendation, the Bonebreakers meet Vaessa Silvertread, the elven captain of the civil guard. At first stern, she softens at the sight of Longtooth’s letter. Under martial law, the Bonebreakers are permitted to enter Arkeus’ tower — and keep anything they find. “Three groups have gone before you,” she warns. “Two never returned. The last came back babbling about clones, melted faces, and madness.” She offers 200 gold per head for proof of Arkeus’ involvement.

They set out along the cliffs as dusk falls. The Tower of Arkeus Whizkeyrd looms ahead — a nightmare of crooked angles and impossible geometry. Chimneys and pipes jut at random; some rooms float unsupported. Animals refuse to approach.

There is no door. No window. Selvar touches the wall and feels a psychic pressure, like thought pushing back. Frank circles around and vanishes — the rest follow, one by one stepping into the shimmer, finding themselves in a pristine hexagonal chamber.

No entrance remains behind them. A single door lies ahead, with an inscription above:

“The leap lies in shadow — step where none would.”

A painting depicts a man fleeing from a mote of light; shelves and a desk line the walls. Athelstan inspects the books, pocketing one referring to instilling sentience. Arden, ever the pragmatist, rolls up the fine rug for later sale.

Frank opens the lone door — beyond lies a corridor of stars, an astral abyss stretching below. As Frank lights a torch, dread washes over them; minds reel. Arden lays the rug over the void — and it floats. Carefully, the Bonebreakers walk across, one by one.

Through the next doorway, they enter a star-shaped chamber, where two crystalline statues stand sentinel. On the wall, a mural depicts a robed figure channeling light into weapons. The statues turn their heads in eerie unison and speak:

“Two minds must echo — harmony opens the path.”

Selvar and Ulrich step forward, puzzled. The puzzle begins: they must each say one word, six times, without coordination, and hope to match.

“Crab.”  
 “Repeat.”

They swap, again and again — five rounds of absolute nonsense — until, on the sixth attempt, their voices align perfectly. The statues hum in resonance, the air vibrates, and two hidden passages slide open behind them.

## Session 27 \- Reflections of the Mind 

Selvar and Ulrich led the way into one of the newly revealed corridors, finding a long chamber lined with tall glass display cases. Inside each sat strange objects.

Barny discovered a tall white candle whose flame burned without motion, its light utterly still. Aethelstan found a lone leather glove displayed like a relic. Selvar’s eyes caught a pewter tankard labeled The Drinker’s Babel, shimmering faintly. Ulrich found a gold coin that, when spun, revealed a new divine face with each turn. Arden noticed a trembling glass inkwell, and Luthien stared at a twitching short sword marked The Laughing Blade.

As the party examined the exhibits, a melted, half-humanoid figure dragged itself into the room. Athlestan raised his holy symbol, and the creature melted back into the floor with a hiss.

In the northern end of the room, one case had exploded, a black fissure torn through the wall beyond.

Meanwhile, Selvar — unable to resist temptation — smashed his display and seized the tankard. An animated book fluttered in from the dark, quill scratching furiously as it began to take notes on Selvar’s every move. When Barny wrote in it, the book retaliated by casting a spell, rendering him invisible.

Selvar took a sip from the Drinker’s Babel, but the liquid simply vanished mid-swallow. Arden handed the trembling inkwell to Barny, who opened it — unleashing a screeching wail that stunned half the group. The ink then wrote a message on its own:

 “You forgot to search the entrance room.”

Chastened, Selvar asked the book to draw a map, and it obliged.

Barny claimed the motionless candle, and immediately every light in the chamber went out — save for its calm, unwavering flame. Aethelstan donned the twitching glove; Ulrich struggled with his display until he pried the case open with his shield, the golden coin spinning to reveal the faces of gods unknown. Luthien, upon taking the sword, began to hear manic laughter in her head — the blade whispering awful jokes she couldn’t help but laugh at.

As Athlestan flexed his new glove, a vivid memory not his own struck him: The King of Ghouls is in the Westmarches. Conveniently, the party had just obtained a map of tombs in that very land.

Suddenly, an unseen force tugged at Arden’s sling, but when Ulrich swung at the air, nothing happened. Searching the cluttered wall, Ulrich found a brass lever; when pulled, a hidden door opened to reveal a room beyond a glowing forcefield.

Ulrich spun his divine coin once more — a new, unfamiliar godly visage appeared. When he prayed to it, a quiet voice whispered:

“Seek another path.”

The group split — Arden, Bran, Aethelstan, and Timo passed through the northern fissure, where a psychic wave rolled through them. Their minds grew sluggish. Meanwhile, Selvar, Ulrich, Luthien, and Barny took the long route, passing through an abandoned reception room: an extinguished hearth, and a dead half-elf slumped in a chair, his weapons missing, bruises deep. They found silver candlesticks, a snuff box, a box of tea, and even took the woven rug.

Reuniting with the others, they entered a furniture workshop — half-built chairs and cabinets floating in mid-air, frozen mid-assembly. Two identical corpses lay on the ground. Barny examined the bench, spotting a glass mallet etched with runes, but when he (and the others in turn) touched it, a violent shock struck him, Timo, and Arden alike. Using a plank, they scooped the mallet into Arden’s pack.

Following the inkwell’s scribbled command, they returned to the starting chamber, taking psychic damage again as they crossed the astral corridor. Searching more thoroughly this time, Selvar rifled through the drawers and found the translucent tuning fork that Professor Longtooth had described — its surface inscribed with planar runes. When he struck it, the stones of the tower quivered, and as he struck it again, the whole room rippled like water.

Back in the workshop, they took the western door, looping south. Luthien pressed her ear to a door, hearing muttering within. Barny slipped in invisible, finding a vast laboratory filled with green-glowing vats, each holding a pale, half-formed figure. In the southern row, the figures bore uncanny resemblance to the Bonebreakers themselves.

At the centre stood three assistants and a frail, ink-stained wizard muttering about “imperfections in the flesh” and “waxy skin.” It was clear — Arkeus Whizkeyrd, or at least, one of him.

When confronted, Arkeus seemed indifferent, more annoyed than afraid. “Nothing is working,” he snapped. Selvar produced the tuning fork. “Ah,” said Arkeus, eyes gleaming. “Bring me the Harmonic Regulator from the detainment room — the one sealed behind the forcefield — and I’ll tell you how to use it. Without it, you’ll never cross the Threshold Gate.”

The Bonebreakers agreed — though Athlestan, ever curious, pulled a failsafe lever on a central dais before leaving. One of the vats went dark.

The clones attacked. Ulrich raised his symbol, blessing the party; Timo’s hypnotic patterns pacified many of the clones, and Barny hastily bargained with the clone of Arkeus to keep his end of the deal.

They pressed west into a colossal library, the air alive with fluttering tomes and errant magic. Books snapped and hissed as they passed. Arden was bitten by one, Ulrich found nothing divine, and Barny and Luthien gathered arcane fragments. Selvar pocketed a volume titled A Treatise on the Sentience of Teapots.

At the far end stood a cage of swirling spells — webs, colour sprays, and more. When Timo approached, it shimmered violently. Barny was flung backward, stunned. Luthien managed to snatch a flying book midair — a scroll of Protection from Lycanthropes.

Arden, ever bold, looped a rope around the cage to pull it aside. Magic detonated. Clairvoyance struck him, and his vision tunneled through the void — seeing the real Arkeus, suspended midair, bound by astral light, two crystal golems patrolling nearby.

Ulrich pulled next and was hit by Ventriloquism, making the clones in the lab sound as if they were begging for release. Finally, Barny yanked the cage aside — and floated upward, caught by Levitate.

Beyond lay two locked doors and, farther south, a vast 100-foot hall split by a shimmering wall — the Threshold Gate. Selvar struck the tuning fork against it, and the barrier rippled, then dissolved.

The Bonebreakers stepped through.

Inside, they found a hexagonal chamber, the air heavy with astral light. Arkeus Whizkeyrd himself hung suspended in the centre — gaunt, ragged, tethered by glowing strands to the stone around him, his body acting as a living anchor.

On either side, two massive crystal golems turned their heads in unison — faceless, luminous, and waiting.

## Session 28 \- From Stars to Blood

In the heart of the astral chamber, the Bonebreakers faced the truth of Arkeus Whizkeyrd’s folly. The wizard hung suspended between worlds, tendrils of light binding him to reality, while two towering crystal golems stood sentinel.

The golems spoke first — their voices like grinding glass: *“He serves penance for crossing too many realms. The motes hunger for form. The wizard is their bridge. He must remain, or the tear will widen.”*

Barny, Athlestan, and Ulrich pressed for clarity, but their answers came in riddles. Ulrich noticed their weapons glowing faintly — the motes of light had nested within them. Selvar, curious, tried to grasp one of the floating motes. It sank briefly into his chest, twisting his movements and his mind before bursting free, leaving him shaken.

Deciding to complete their deal with the clone of Arkeus, the Bonebreakers set out to retrieve the Harmonics Regulator. They retraced their steps to the north-east halls, where Selvar unlocked a sealed door with a sharp Knock spell. Inside was an animated kitchen, pots and pans whirling in a dance of invisible cooks while several clones sat slack-jawed, eating stew in eerie silence. Selvar prodded one with his blade — no reaction.

Beyond, they found a metal-walled chamber, the long-awaited room split by a humming forcefield. Selvar struck the barrier with the tuning fork, and like the Threshold Gate before it, it shimmered and dissolved.

Within floated the objects of interest — a jagged pale dagger, a heavy fluttering tome, and the crystalline mass of rods and prisms that made up the Harmonics Regulator.

Athlestan seized the device while Barny reached for the tome. It spoke to him in a withering, arrogant voice. “Who dares?”  
 “I am Barnabuck the Bizarre,” he announced proudly.  
 “Prove it.”  
 “I’m invisible,” he retorted.  
 The book grew irritable, turning invisible itself and casting Hold Person on him in revenge.

Meanwhile, Frank reached for the dagger. It pulsed in his mind — visions of glory, conquest, and dominion flooding his thoughts. He saw himself rising to power, ruling not just Ikiria but the world. Its whisper was intoxicating.

Barny’s paralysis faded just as Frank retrieved the fallen tome. The book snapped, “You’re not my master,” before Barny snatched it back — only for it to cast Sleep on him this time. Rhian calmly took the book, which immediately changed tone: “Ah, a more respectful hand.” Frank woke Barny with a slap, earning only fury in return.

With the regulator secured, the Bonebreakers returned to the Threshold Gate. Above it, a brass platform bristled with levers and pipes. Selvar pulled one — it snapped, and the machine groaned to a halt. He and Luthien stayed behind to repair it, while the others went to deliver the regulator to Clone Arkeus.

Passing the unbound spells swirling in the library, Ulrich and Aethelstan chose to hold back. The others pressed forward — and an arcane burst detonated, hurling them to the floor. Somewhere far beyond the tower, the sea itself was torn apart by the unintended effect of the released magic — a Lower Water spell of immense magnitude.

Regaining their feet, Barny and company found Clone Arkeus and lured him back toward the Threshold Gate. Athlestan, clutching the Harmonics Regulator, refused to hand it over without answers. Arkeus, losing patience, lunged for it — and a comically frantic scuffle broke out. The two wrestled across the chamber, the wizard snatching and sprinting away, the cleric barreling after him.

At last, panting, they reached a stalemate. The Bonebreakers pressed him: “You’re not the real Arkeus. You’re his shadow.” He denied it furiously — until they dragged him before the true Arkeus, still suspended midair in the astral light.

Clone Arkeus hesitated — then rushed forward, pulling his original free. With a wet *pop*, the old wizard fell to the ground, and the air split open. A portal to the Astral Plane yawned wide. The two Arkeuses were drawn into it bodily. As he vanished, the real wizard gave a weary smile.

“Look after the tower, won’t you?”

The rift expanded, pulling every mote, clone, and sentient object into its void. The tower grew still — except for the two crystal golems, who turned their gaze on the Bonebreakers.

Battle erupted. Arden blessed the party, Barny webbed the constructs, and Timo conjured mirror images. Frank’s bolts ricocheted off one as Bran’s blade shattered its arm. Athlestan charged in, smashing a golem to shards, and Frank delivered the killing blow to the other.

When silence fell, they collected gleaming gems from the golems’ remains and searched for escape. Selvar’s enchanted book suggested: *“Stand where you began.”*

Back in the first room, Arden confidently walked straight into a wall. No effect. Recalling the rug they’d taken earlier, they unrolled it and stood upon it — and in an instant, the tower vanished around them.

They reappeared at the cliffside outside Ikiria, the wind in their hair, the madness of the tower behind them.

At the Flux Academy, Professor Longtooth greeted them in disbelief and relief. Barny recounted a wildly embellished tale of noble sacrifice — his version of events far more heroic (and inaccurate) than reality — but even he admitted Arkeus had gone too far.

True to her word, Longtooth granted each a reward and access to the Academy’s inner vaults.

* Selvar took a spell scroll.  
* Ulrich claimed a \+1 mace.  
* Barny chose a Staff of Withering.  
* Frank and Arden each took rings of protection \+1.

Leaving the Academy, they found chaos in the harbor — ships smashed against the seabed, the ocean itself drained away by the very spell that had torn free in the tower.

That night, they rested. Frank took a brief leave, calling in his duergar associates Akal and Del to join the Bonebreakers. Arden, needing recovery, stepped aside, replaced by the young street urchin Tess Tattercloak, “saved” by Sir Cedric, and a bright-eyed halfling adventurer named Tobold Took.

But peace did not last.

In the dark of night, Barny awoke drenched in sweat, his dreams haunted by dying roses and creeping shadows. He gasped awake — and the next morning, Professor Longtooth’s summons arrived once more.

At the Academy, she introduced a terrified, half-naked young man — Arun, a noble’s son. Through trembling words, he described a castle that appeared outside Ikiria, filled with monsters and tortured humans. From his satchel, he produced a rotting rose, identical to those in Barny’s nightmare.

Tobold comforted the boy — until the rose drank his blood from a careless prick. Akal muttered about profit in rescuing nobles, while Tess eagerly asked if their families were rich. Arun’s eyes fixed on Barny — noticing two small punctures on his neck.

Guided by Arun, they journeyed to the castle’s outskirts. Night had fallen, and a blood-red moon hung above. A wrought-iron fence surrounded the grounds, mist curling along its base. Two armored figures stood by a chest at the gate. Arun fled, terrified.

The guards demanded an invitation. Akal tried a ruse, claiming to deliver a captive human, but when the deception failed, steel was drawn. One guard dipped his sword into the chest — a basin of blood.

The fight was brutal. Akal struck first, Del’s duergar mindfire heating armor red-hot, and Tobold’s blood-soaked blade twisted inside his foe. Tess unleashed a Chromatic Orb, burning one guard, while the other broke free of enchantment and begged for mercy. He revealed he was once a commoner, paid by a noble and enslaved by the castle’s magic.

Akal listened — then cut his throat. Tess searched the bodies, finding nothing but rust and blood.

When Luthien inspected the mole-like iron gate, it snapped at her hand, biting down. Tess jabbed it with a pole — it bit that too. Finally, Del found a key on one of the corpses.

The lock turned.

## Session 29 \- The Blood Moon Rises

The Bonebreakers stepped beneath the crimson moon and through the iron gate of the vampire’s domain, where the air itself seemed to hum with dread.

Tobold Took, ever the brave (or foolish), took the lead along a black stone path lined with rotting roses. Classical piano music floated through the mist from the looming castle ahead. But before long, a low growl broke through the melody — three great hounds, each the size of a man, eyes glowing red.

Tobold loosed an arrow dipped in the strange blood found at the gate. It struck true — and the beasts lunged. Their tongues lashed out like whips, one coiling around him and crushing tight. The rest of the Bonebreakers surged forward — Athlestan’s mace blazed, Barny’s staff of withering cracked through decayed hide, and Luthien’s blade finished one cleanly. The creatures bled not at all — undead.

Athlestan raised the holy symbol of Karanth, and the hounds recoiled and fled, howling into the fog. He then knelt to heal Tobold’s crushed ribs.

While the others caught their breath, Tess Tattercloak spotted a bent section of fence, slipping through to investigate. She found a charred corpse — a priest, judging by his scorched robes, the metal of the fence partially melted nearby. Looting with zeal, she found two vials of holy water, a ring (which she promptly donned to no effect), and 50 gold pieces.

The party crept along the western façade of the manor. Six tall stained-glass windows glowed faintly red from within. Del peered through the third and saw a room of gold and velvet, murals showing vampires feasting. Through the next two, he glimpsed a ransacked armory, three steel-armoured statues standing at attention, visors down. The sixth window was barricaded, and Luthien heard muffled moaning behind it.

Rounding the corner, they reached the main door, a massive slab of oak with a painted yellow eye staring out. The piano music stopped. When Barny jabbed the painted pupil, nothing happened. Athlestan took a more direct approach — he smashed the nearby window, climbed through, and the Bonebreakers followed.

Inside lay a cramped dormitory lined with bunks, each neatly made. A distant scream echoed through the eastern halls. Searching, Athlestan found a letter beneath a pillow — addressed to Arun, the noble boy who had guided them here. It was from Elara, a lover left behind, fearful that he had become one of the dark riders from the manor she’d seen on the roads.

Tess ransacked the dresser, but found nothing of value.

Through the next door stretched a long corridor, lit by candelabras and lined with paintings of strange, unsettling scenes — all still, yet uncanny. The carpet beneath their feet was deep red, soft and silent underfoot. Tobold unbarred the back door from the inside to keep their escape open.

Exploring a side room, Luthien found an iron gate and descending stairs, the walls pulsating faintly with red-veined stone. A fungal stench hung in the air. It led down.

Athlestan muttered a prayer and cast his new spell, Ghoul Diviner. His vision burned white. The strongest undead presence lay directly above them. Tess shrieked, looking up — thinking it was on the ceiling — before realizing otherwise.

In an adjacent chamber, Tess crept in first. A light flared to life — not from her hand, but from a source unseen. The room was a tangle of traps — tripwires, crossbows, spikes, and shattered furniture. From the shadows, a pale armored woman hissed, “One more step and I’ll stake you where you stand\!”

A pale vampire sat bound behind her, eyes pleading. Barny raised his hands. “We’re here to kill vampires, not join them.”

The woman relaxed — slightly. She introduced herself as Selana, one of a long-lost party who had come here to hunt the Blood King. Her companions were slain in the great hall, and she had been trapped ever since. She fed from the vampire to survive, though she herself was not undead.

She told them grimly what she’d learned: there were at least a dozen vampires in the castle, and worse things besides. The Blood King was far more powerful than the rest, and could only be killed by destroying his heart, hidden somewhere deep within the manor. The key, she believed, lay in the southeast wing. She also described the guard quarters to the southwest.

When asked where she had found the castle, her description didn’t match its current location — it seemed to move, shifting through the world like a phantom.

The Bonebreakers agreed to an alliance.

But before plans could be made, another scream tore through the corridor. Tess peeked out and saw five armored figures dragging three prisoners.

The Bonebreakers charged.  
Athlestan’s Hold Person froze two. Tess and Tobold cut into another; Barny’s staff withered a man to dust, aging him decades in a heartbeat. Del struck hard, and Tess finished one with a dagger to the throat. Tobold’s sword drank deeply, and Athlestan crushed the last with divine fury.

Panting, they looked down — and saw the carpet drinking the blood, its texture rippling like a tongue.

Tess looted the corpses eagerly, finding 10 gold. Tobold, grim-faced, returned to the trapped room and staked the bound vampire, who dissolved into mist — then to nothing. Barny finished the paralysed guards with his staff, aging them forty years in an instant.

Luthien checked the armory next — the same one Del had glimpsed. It was in ruins, already plundered. Tess, determined, heaved at one of the heavy statues. It toppled with a crash — nothing stirred.

Then, from a crack in the wall, a procession of spiders — neat, deliberate, marching in line — crawled out and vanished. Barny stabbed one absently. They did not react.

Selana led the group south, into the entry hall. The massive gold-filigreed doors loomed ahead, candles flickering low. In the corner stood a dwarven statue, hand extended as if awaiting an offering. Opposite it, a coat stand hung with bloodstained garments. Ahead, iron double doors, smeared in crimson, led into the manor’s central chamber.

The party pressed on through the southeast corridor, and Athlestan opened a side door — into a strange little room packed with hundreds of hats. Mirrors lined the walls, one huge and unbroken at the center.

Barny couldn’t resist. He donned a hat — and grew claws. The mirror’s surface rippled, and a voice echoed:

“Who dares disturb me?”

Barny straightened. “Barnobuck the Bizarre\!”

The figure in the mirror was regal, sad-eyed, with amethyst irises and a rose crest upon his fine tunic. “I am Alvalus,” he said. “All that the Blood King cast away — his guilt, his regret, his shame. I am his reflection, bound within this glass.”

He told them the truth: if they showed the Blood King this mirror, he would tremble with fear. But his minions would surely try to destroy it first.

Tess, delighted, found herself a hat of her own — something suitably dramatic — and the Bonebreakers resolved to use the mirror when the time was right.

As they stepped back into the corridor, blood began to stream down the walls, and several felt their stomachs turn. Selana opened the next door — a guest chamber, reeking of torture and old blood. A hulking armoire crouched in the corner, its drawers lined with teeth.

Tess pried at it with a pole, showing surprising strength, but it snapped at her. Athlestan smashed it apart, revealing a key bearing a rose crest, and an ivory comb.

Tess grinned, ordering him to break the rest. Inside were fine gothic garments, perfumed faintly with rose and blood. She quickly dressed herself in them — no longer a scruffy street urchin, but a proper lady of the night.

## Interlude I, Part I — “The Stench Below”

Far from the Bonebreakers’ crusades, a new tale began — one of greed, filth, and poor decision-making. In a distant inland city, a crooked band of adventurers gathered beneath the streets: Snipe the elf, Scamp and Cherry the halflings, Blaine the cleric, and Sarge the fighter.

The Sewer Guildmaster told them of Hal, a worker who’d found a break in the great tunnels — and been dragged screaming into something ancient below. Smelling coin, the party descended.

At the site, they found a lever; Snipe pulled it, opening a grate to deeper tunnels, and Scamp wedged it open. Beyond a collapsed wall lay sea-themed mosaics and bloody drag marks, which they promptly ignored, heading south instead.

A side room proved to be a wine cellar. Cherry pocketed a magically preserved bottle. West of there, Blaine accidentally uncovered a secret door to the main sewer, and further south, they entered a circular chamber—only to be hit by a wave of stench as four troglodytes leapt from the dark.

The fight was swift and brutal: Blaine, Cherry, and Scamp were torn apart, while Snipe and Sarge barely survived, slaying the last of the beasts before fleeing the sewers.

They soon returned with new blood — Higgley the halfling, Gordo the magic-user, and Greedo the dwarf — and retraced their path through the secret entrance. Eastward, they found a crushed troglodyte beneath fallen stone, and beyond that, six more sleeping. The group quietly doused the room in oil and burned them alive, killing four before the others escaped.

Higgley looted coins and silver bracelets, and they pressed on into a candle-lit hexagonal chamber with a maggot statue, swearing to return for it later.

Next, they met Malarian the Unwashed, a ragged priest of the maggot god, with a tiny pet Carcass Crawler squirming beside him. When he raised his wand, the party struck first. Both priest and creature died swiftly. Gordo claimed the Wand of Fetid Curses, and they scavenged an unknown potion before moving on.

In a nearby library, Greedo took a fine rug while the others found rotting books on decay and the Sicilia family, whose buried estate this seemed to be. Beyond a ruined bathhouse, their hammering drew more troglodytes — and this time Snipe fell, cut down in the dark.

As the echoes faded, the surviving scoundrels stood among corpses and dripping stone, the stench of rot thick around them — and somewhere deeper, something in the dark whispered approval.

## Interlude I, Part II — “The Maw Below”

The survivors of the sewer delve weren’t done with death just yet. With the wall finally broken open to daylight, Gordo, Sarge, Higgley, and the Bonesmith sought reinforcements. Three souls — or what passed for them — answered the call: The Hollow One, Min the Dwarf, and the grim Bonesmith. Together they returned to the dripping tunnels, heading west toward the old pillared hall.

Two sleeping troglodytes barred their path — briefly. The party dispatched them with brutal efficiency and moved on to the chamber with the pit, where a rickety ladder descended into darkness. They decided to explore further west first — a choice that nearly cost them all.

A giant black widow spider, thick as a horse, dropped from above. Greedo was bitten before anyone could react, its venom claiming him swiftly. The group avenged him in kind, filling the corridor with steel and spells until the spider lay twitching. From its lair, they scavenged what trinkets they could before returning to the pit.

Rather than risk the ladder, Higgley tied a rope to Greedo’s corpse, lowering it as a counterweight — and, grimly, themselves after. They descended into a vast cavern heaped with corpses, the air thick with rot and the faint hum of insects. As they sifted through the dead, one body stirred — a living human. Luck, a rogue who’d somehow survived the pile, coughed herself free and joined their ill-fated venture.

Among the remains they found a scattering of treasures, and a northern tunnel leading to an alcove where three troglodytes waited — one of them larger, armed, and mean-eyed. Mukklah Tuk, their leader. Gordo raised her Wand of Fetid Curses, uttered a spell of charm, and the beast’s expression softened. Mukklah bowed his head, now her loyal ally. Pointing east with a claw, he rasped, “Hal went that way.”

The group followed, stepping into a cavern vast enough to swallow a cathedral. There, in the flickering torchlight, they saw Hal’s mangled body — and behind it, a colossal maggot, sixty feet long, its pale hide pulsing with veins of rot.

The Maggot God.

Sarge, foolhardy and brave, stepped forward to recover Hal’s corpse — and the creature surged to life. It lunged, its maw opening wide enough to engulf him. The chamber erupted into chaos.

Higgley, screaming defiance, charged straight into the beast’s mouth, stabbing from within as acid hissed around him. The Bonesmith hurled flasks of high-proof spirits, setting its eyes ablaze. The Hollow One vaulted a ledge and leapt down, slamming his weapon into its back with a sickening crunch. Gordo fired her wand — it fizzled — and resorted to throwing daggers instead.

The maggot reared, screaming, spewing bile. Higgley dissolved within, bones and blade both consumed. Sarge was struck dead as the beast’s bulk crashed upon him. But before it could feed again, Luck nocked an arrow and fired — the shaft pierced deep, and the Maggot God erupted, bursting apart in a rain of gore that sent the survivors sprawling.

When the silence settled, they looted what remained, panting amid the viscera. Their work was not done — Mukklah Tuk and his troglodytes arrived, eager to claim the carnage. Thinking quickly, Gordo proclaimed herself prophet of the Demon Frog, convincing Mukklah to forsake the maggot and build a new cult in the swamps. He bowed, and she smiled — already planning her next empire.

The survivors limped from the sewers, collected their gold from the guildmaster, and vanished into the city streets — another chapter of filth and foolish glory sealed beneath the earth.

## Session 30 – A Toast to the Damned

Back in the cursed manor, the Bonebreakers pressed on — weary, bloodstained, and now dressed like their prey. Luthien draped one of the vampires’ dark cloaks about her shoulders, its silken folds cool and heavy. Selana sniffed the air, remarking that she now smelled like one of them. The rest of the party, not ones to waste an advantage, donned the cloaks too, until the whole group looked ready for an unholy banquet.

Then Akal returned — somewhat disheveled, muttering about having “used his powers to run around tiny for a few hours.” He’d been exploring, he said, and had glimpsed what looked like a games room, and what he thought were ghosts. Before anyone could question him further, the sound of shattering glass echoed from nearby.

The Bonebreakers crept toward the noise, finding themselves in a trophy hall, a long chamber lined with silver cups, gilt medals, and portraits of pale nobility. A crowned vampire statue stood in pride of place, overlooking a polished mahogany bar still stocked with bottles. And at that bar sat a lone figure — a drunken vampire, slumped and muttering into his goblet.

Sensing opportunity, Akal whispered a plan to Del, and the two Duergar swaggered in, feigning inebriation. They shared a toast with the undead noble, who, in his stupor, grew chatty. Between slurred words and bloody chuckles, he revealed two key secrets: that the Vampire King wears a relic about his neck capable of resurrecting the dead, and that Lord Demetrius, another of the manor’s vampiric lords, never drinks blood at all.

Once the vampire had outlived his usefulness, the Bonebreakers struck. Steel flashed; the creature hissed, dissolving into mist, only to re-form moments later as a snarling wolf, pinning Barny beneath its claws. But before it could finish him, Del drove a stake through its heart, ending it in a spasm of dark smoke and silence.

Behind the bar, Barny found a bottle containing two disembodied eyes, still blinking, watching the group. He shook it violently — the eyes spun dizzily within, and he pocketed it with satisfaction. The party helped themselves to trophies and fine bottles of aged wine, before slipping through a side door.

They emerged into a vast glass-ceilinged conservatory, the air humid, filled with overgrown flowers and creeping vines that pulsed faintly in the candlelight. Then, movement — enormous spiders scuttled down from the trellises, hissing. “Murderers\!” they cried in high, chittering voices.

Battle erupted among the blossoms. The Bonebreakers cut one spider down quickly, but Tess took a brutal hit, vanishing with a flicker as her invisibility spell took hold. The remaining spiders retreated, shouting in panic as they scurried into the shadows — “We must tell the queen\!”

The conservatory fell still again, the scent of crushed roses and blood heavy in the air. The Bonebreakers caught their breath, blades wet and nerves taut, knowing now that this cursed manor held not just vampires… but something else waiting too.

## Session 31 – Blood in the Bath, Knives in the Dark

The Bonebreakers begin by harvesting the strange arcane lotus flowers in the glass-roofed garden, pocketing several before moving on. Through a north-eastern door they enter an immaculate music room dominated by a pure silver grand piano. Sheet music rests nearby, and on the desk Tess finds a letter addressed to the Blood King’s daughter. Though unsigned, it is clearly from Lord Demetrius—pledging support against the King and hinting that a useful artifact has been hidden within the piano itself.

Before they can act on this, a bookcase swings open and the Blood King’s daughter enters, flanked by Demetrius. She calmly judges the party and makes her offer: aid her ascension, and they will be spared when she becomes Queen. As proof of loyalty, she orders them to assassinate Circander, a vampire who threatens to expose her secrets at the coming feast—conveniently vulnerable while bathing. The party agrees, at least for now. While attention is elsewhere, Tess slips away invisibly and steals a finely wrought obsidian dagger.

Exploring west, the Bonebreakers find a barracks filled with footlockers containing love poems devoted to the Princess of Blood, along with a platinum mirror. Beyond that lies an opulent bathing chamber: six golden tubs, murals of vampires feeding, and Circander herself reclining in blood. The attack is swift and brutal—holy water poured into the tub, blades driven home, and when she tries to escape, Barny trips her. Tess breaks invisibility, drags her back, and stakes her cleanly through the heart. Circander dissolves into mist, but the blood in the neighbouring bath rises into a living trap, forcing the party to flee.

Returning to the Princess, they are rewarded with a wand (given to Barny), a key to the basement, and a map of the upper floor. She promises that everything will be resolved at the feast.

The party presses on, finding a bunkroom holding three human guards. Shaken awake, one explains that the feast is imminent and the dungeons are full. Barny drains his life with the Staff of Withering, killing him outright. Tess finds a magical crossbow and hands it to Luthien. The remaining guards are slain—one in his sleep, the other after a brief struggle—before a dark shadow sweeps through, snuffing out all light. As they leave, Barny discreetly raises one corpse as a zombie.

In a lavish bedroom nearby, a ghostly woman weeps. She tells them her son, Serion, was taken and infused with the Blood King’s power, begging the party to find him. They promise to try. While she mourns, Luthien smashes open an ornate chest, claiming jewellery worth thousands of gold.

Descending into the basement, the Bonebreakers find a torture chamber with cages full of prisoners. Freed captives reveal the Blood King has been torturing a vampire in the next room. Inside, the party finds a battered figure resembling Lord Demetrius—but speaking with it reveals something far worse: the body is host to a sentient magical fungus seeking to spread itself into the world as a hive mind. Pretending to agree, the party instead douses the creature in oil and burns it, destroying this fragment of the infestation, though its true reach remains unknown.

On the way out, Luthien discovers a trove of valuables: a large dark key, scrolls of *Remove Curse* and *Protection from Evil*, enchanted gloves, and an unknown potion. Barny dons the gloves and realises they grant knowledge of the age of anything he touches.

Gathering the rescued prisoners, the Bonebreakers retreat back to Selana’s fortified room, knowing the feast is close—and the castle’s secrets are only beginning to surface.

## Session 32 – The Heart of the Night

Leaving the rescued prisoners barricaded safely in Selana’s trapped room with what rations they can spare, the Bonebreakers push deeper into the manor. Their next stop is the kitchens: a long, grisly chamber where slabs of unmistakably human meat lie butchered across tables, blood pooling beneath. Three vacant-eyed servants work methodically, chopping and draining, barely aware of their surroundings.

Barny slips into invisibility and quietly poisons the goblets of blood being prepared for the feast, while Luthien helps herself to the silverware. A door to the west reveals an opulent dining hall beyond—long tables, fine place settings, and a chandelier glittering above an obscene banquet prepared for vampires. Tess climbs effortlessly, stripping every crystal from the chandelier just as footsteps echo nearby.

Retreating back through the kitchens, the party hears cries from behind an eastern door. Inside, caged humans—including a terrified young girl—cry out for help. The servants attack as Luthien struggles with the locks. Steel flashes: Luthien and Del cut one down, Rose vaults and kills another in a spectacular leap, and Tess nearly dies finishing the last before Luthien ends it. A rusty key and a handful of gold are taken from the bodies, and the prisoners are freed and escorted to safety. Tess takes the girl’s hand herself.

Tess samples the strange black lotus she harvested earlier, feeling oddly renewed as magical strength floods back into her.

Seeking the Blood King’s final weakness, Luthien casts *Locate Object* on the lock said to fit his heart. The spell draws them upward, narrowing its source to the eastern upper wing—either the observatory or the princess’s chambers.

They ascend a narrow staircase of warped, subtly shifting wood and emerge onto a vast balcony open to the night sky. A massive telescope dominates one end, while a towering orchid with a swollen, perfumed bloom waits at the other. Luthien cuts into it, releasing a heavy, intoxicating scent that arouses her and Tess. Refusing to risk further manipulation, the party destroys the carnivorous plant in a brutal skirmish, Selana taking grievous wounds before it finally falls. Barny tests the telescope and realises it reveals the recent nightmares of whoever it is aimed at.

Pressing on, the party enters the observatory proper—a soaring chamber mirroring the heavens. At its centre floats a vast, rotating model of the cosmos, bathed in blood-red light. Tess examines a tome on a pedestal, discovering it contains texts in many languages, including passages in Draconic concerning political events across the world.

Realising the planetary model represents their own reality, Tess impulsively pulls a lever. Lights stutter. A keyhole irises open in the central star. Luthien inserts the key.

The room erupts.

The planets scream into motion, energy lashing outward. Tess, Del, and Barny are nearly killed outright. Selana, already weakened, is struck down and dies. As the system slows, the star opens to reveal a massive, beating heart—the Blood King’s true core. Without hesitation, the party drives their stakes into it. After one final, terrible pulse, the heart falls still.

The manor begins to shudder.

With collapse imminent, the Bonebreakers grab what they can: Tess tears free the smallest planet—Mercury—from the model and takes the tome; Barny shoulders the telescope; Luthien lifts Selana’s body. As the halls convulse, Tess and Luthien race back for the prisoners while the others ambush five pursuing guards in the kitchens.

They flee through the rear of the manor, racing for the melted breach in the fence as stone cracks and walls pulse behind them. Looking back only once, they escape as the Halls of the Blood King begin to tear themselves apart.

The heart is destroyed, and whatever held the castle together is finally dying.

## Session 33 – The Taking of Tobold Took

The Bonebreakers flee the collapsing manor with the freed prisoners as dawn breaks. The Blood Moon fades to a harvest moon, then to full daylight—and with it comes the realisation that it is the morning of the festival day.

Travelling south toward Ikiria, they pass a small village. Tobold, ever eager for food, runs ahead—just as a vast shadow passes overhead. A giant hawk swoops down, snatches him up, and carries him west at terrifying speed. The party gives chase but quickly loses it. The villagers confirm this horror is new: children have been taken the same way, always from the west and back toward it. The Bonebreakers agree to help.

Leaving the prisoners in the villagers’ care, they borrow horses and ride west, finding another village with the same grim story. Realising they need preparation, they return the prisoners to Ikiria and rest at the Temple, where Arden, Sir Cedric, and other healers are present. Research in the library—and confirmation from a pagan woodsman—reveals that giant hawks can only be so coordinated if highly trained, something unheard of outside rare circumstances. Rumours point to elves, though this contradicts what is known of the region.

Digging deeper, the party uncovers old histories: over 2,000 years ago Westmarsh was a thriving land of culture and learning, abandoned after a necrotic plague. Agria was founded by those who fled east. What remains in Westmarsh now is largely unknown.

With Tobold taken and children vanishing, the Bonebreakers plan a western expedition—via Barrow Spa, possibly stopping at the Elven lands south of it, and onward to Westfort. They travel west from Ikiria, pass the Church, deposit funds in Barrow Spa, liquidate mundane loot, and continue along the West Road.

On the road, they encounter a lone rider moving fast. To the shock of several companions, Akal attacks without hesitation. Selvar casts *Sleep*; the rider falls, and Akal kills him. The body yields an illegal dagger, a bottle of liquid, and a book in Gnollish. Deciphered, it proves to be a record of gnoll raids and human ransoms. Ulrich is openly disgusted; Tess, shaken, drags the body into the bushes.

They reach Westfort—a crumbling stone ruin reinforced with wooden palisades. Guards halt them at the gate, warning of nearby dangers, until Tess explains their mission to find the kidnapped children. Inside, they find a struggling town of around 400 people. The armoury is bare, the barracks undermanned.

They are brought before Sergeant Dara, a hard-eyed veteran who has little patience for adventurers. Akal’s attempted bribe earns only a glare, but when Tess and Selvar explain the kidnappings—and Tobold’s abduction—she listens. Dara reveals that the night after the children were taken, the fort was sabotaged: the granary burned, the water poisoned, and a large cache of weapons stolen. Support is failing.

Akal offers twelve swords in trade. Despite her clear dislike of him, Dara accepts, desperately needing arms. In return, she grants the party use of Westfort as a base and a Westmarsh map drawn by Kenric.

The Bonebreakers settle into the Cracked Shield, a weathered inn run by Osric, a wary barkeep who has seen too much. Tess slips into invisibility to eavesdrop, overhearing troubling rumours: hobgoblins hiring for raids, gnolls growing bolder near the bridge, and monsters acting with unusual coordination—as if directed.

Luthien visits a small library, learning that Westmarsh teems with gnolls on hyenas, orcs, goblins, bugbears, ogres, and undead. Akal’s questions uncover another detail: witnesses saw human mercenaries fleeing the fort the night of the raid—efficient, disciplined, and very much alive.

Ulrich visits the local wooden temple, meeting Sister Aldrith, a compassionate cleric of St Lucia the Merciful. She offers healing, sells holy water, and expresses keen interest in undead samples and ancient texts or relics.

At Kenric’s Cartography, the party receives one map freely and commissions another. Tess attempts—unsuccessfully—to steal the payment back and wisely gives up. Finally, they speak with Captain Rodrick about flushing out the weapon thieves, but he dismisses the idea, convinced monsters alone are to blame.

## Session 34 – When the Trap Is Yours

A reduced strike party of the Bonebreakers prepares to probe Westmarsh, bolstered by several new faces: Bernard the Businessman, Steve “Ligma” Smith, Quak\! the bard, and Alison the knight. Before departure, they are visited by Commander Valerius, a grizzled and cynical veteran who offers guarded insight into the region. Steve’s antagonism quickly sours the exchange, and Valerius leaves unimpressed.

After a night of preparation and studying newly acquired maps marking monster territories and nearby ruins, the party hires a wagon and draft horse from Goren Heavyhoof, while Bernard and Akal quietly acquire poison. Crossing the ancient bridge out of Westfort—a vast, old span flanked by watchtowers overlooking the western approach—they devise a plan: Tess and Alison will pose as travellers beside the cart, while the rest lie concealed beneath a tarp, disguised among chickens, ready to spring an ambush.

The plan collapses almost immediately.

Nine Gnolls ambush the party first. In a devastating opening volley, Tess is riddled with arrows and killed before anyone can react. Alison charges in fury, and the Bonebreakers surge from hiding. Quak\! casts Entangle, snaring most of the Gnolls, and the party swiftly kills the rest.

What follows is grim. Steve and Akal brutally interrogate the survivors, extracting information through torture. They learn of a Gnoll matriarch named Grazka, somewhere deeper in the marsh. The Gnolls also claim the giant hawks flew south—but the party questions the truth of this. The captives are knocked unconscious.

Returning to Westfort with Tess’s body, they are met again by Commander Valerius, who takes the Gnolls into custody and voices strong doubts about the reliability of the information. Sir Cedric arrives soon after, shaken by Tess’s death, and pays to have her body transported to Barrow Spa for resurrection. Akal contributes 500 gold, burdened by guilt over suggesting she be used as bait.

As the party regroups, rumours circulate: Queen Audrey is aging, and succession tensions between the younger Prince Arthur and the elder Princess Agatha are growing. The Bonebreakers venture west, then south, but caution wins out. During the night, Akal spots goblins lurking at the edge of camp; attempts at communication fail as they scatter into the dark. Quak leaves a grisly offering—a Gnoll head and a promise of meat—to signal peaceful intent, exploiting known hatreds.

With spirits shaken and plans uncertain, the party returns once more to Westfort, aware that Westmarsh is deadlier—and more complicated—than they feared.

## Session 35 – Flames on the Frontier

Back at the Cracked Shield, the Bonebreakers welcomed a new face to the table – Cyder, a freshly graduated magic-user who’d only just scraped through wizard school. The evening was lively, with drink flowing and the ever-flirtatious Sarla hovering nearby, watching the party far more closely than most serving girls ever would.

Elsewhere in the tavern, Akal relieved Private Jordan, a young, drunken soldier with a gambling problem, of his clothes, dignity, and coin. Sir Cedric, true to Belenus’ mercy, gave the poor fool his cape and a gold piece, and helped him stumble back to bed.

When night fell, Akal shrank himself and slipped into the kitchen, with Barny shadowing him. The rest of the party turned in upstairs. Barny stayed awake studying until he heard footsteps above, then a sudden thud – and soon after, the smell of smoke.

The kitchen was ablaze. Someone had set fire to the stacked logs beside the hearth, and the flames were spreading fast.

Akal raised the alarm while Barny charged back inside to rescue the tavern’s cat. Ulrich leapt from a window, Selvar followed, and Steve hauled Cyder out over his shoulder. Sir Cedric fought his way through the smoke to wake Osric, a serving girl named Lyanna, and several merchants. With flames blocking the stairs, Cyder cast Web beneath a window, and Cedric began throwing people to safety – finally grappling Osric and leaping out with him when the stubborn innkeeper refused to jump.

The townsfolk helped douse the fire, but the first floor collapsed entirely. Grateful for their lives, Osric promised the Bonebreakers free food, drink, and lodging for good.

Suspicion quickly fell on Sarla – the only one left behind after closing time, and far too interested in the party’s business. Steve dragged her in for questioning. She broke down, confessing that a man named Vex had forced her to start the fire, threatening to kill her if she refused. When she tried to flee, Cyder dropped her with a Sleep spell.

Commander Valerius arrived, immediately clashing with Steve’s attitude. The party learned Vex operated from a warehouse in town. While the guards marched for it, the Bonebreakers circled around the back.

Vex burst out the rear door straight into them, wounding Cyder before Selvar put him to sleep. Inside the warehouse, the party uncovered crates of swords and shields – the very weapons stolen from West Fort’s barracks.

Under Charm, Vex confessed to everything: burning the granary, poisoning the well, stealing the arms, and torching the inn, all on orders from an unknown hooded figure. The Bonebreakers also relieved him of a hidden stash of 3,000 gold pieces. Worse still, Vex revealed that Veteran Borak, a respected half-orc guard, had been ordered to kill Sarla to silence her.

The party rushed back just in time to see Borak slit Sarla’s throat. Ulrich blinded him with divine light, and Cedric saved Sarla’s life with a desperate healing prayer.

Rather than immediately exposing the conspiracy, the Bonebreakers pitched a bolder plan to Valerius: leave the warehouse untouched, let Vex meet his mysterious employer, and ambush him. Though clearly unimpressed, Valerius agreed – West Fort needed answers.

For several nights, the party lay in wait beneath the great bridge to the Westmarsh, Barny even spying through Vex’s eyes via his Seer’s Dagger. Valerius publicly praised the Bonebreakers for saving the Cracked Shield, while quietly preparing for what was to come.

At last, the hooded figure arrived, crossing the bridge with four orcs in tow. As he approached the gate to speak with Vex, the Bonebreakers struck. Cyder webbed him in place, Cedric tore back his hood to reveal an unfamiliar human face, and Akal and Selvar dropped the orcs with arrows and magic. Barny’s Sleep spell felled the rest – though Steve still managed to claim a grisly trophy.

With the conspirators captured and the orcs bound, the Bonebreakers retreated into West Fort, the shadowy plot against the town finally beginning to unravel.

The Bonebreakers begin by deciding how best to squeeze answers from the hooded man captured at the bridge. Akal searches him, uncovering hidden, poisoned daggers sewn into his shoes, which Rose swiftly claims, along with a cryptic note. The Orc mercenaries are searched as well; they admit they were hired two months ago, know little beyond their pay, and confirm the giant hawks flew south. True to his word, Steve releases one of them—Muzgash—who bolts in terrified confusion. The remaining Orcs are handed over to Sergeant Dara.

Using Vex’s warehouse as a temporary base, Barny charms the hooded man, christening him “Jeremy.” Scarred and nervous, Jeremy admits he pays Vex but is only a middleman. His true handler is a woman named Ash, whom he must meet at dawn at the Spider’s Market west of the fort—or risk exposure. At Barny’s urging, Jeremy allows the Seer’s Dagger to be used on him.

Disguised in cloaks from the warehouse, the party rides hard and reaches the Spider’s Market just after dawn. The place is a tense neutral ground where the monsters of the Westmarsh trade side by side—Orcs, Hobgoblins, Bugbears, Lizardfolk, and worse amid tents and broken stone. Steve, wearing flayed Orc skin, watches as Jeremy meets Ash, a female Orc, and speaks with her in Orcish. The meeting is brief; they agree to meet again the next morning.

The party takes advantage of the market. Steve is compelled to buy a sword he can’t take his eyes off. Akal acquires a vicious shortsword and even a wolf to ride, while Cedric purchases a gleaming shield. Trusting the market’s neutrality, they rest nearby before striking out southeast into the hills.

There, they discover a cave marked by heavy traffic and venture inside, torches raised. Nine Hobgoblins confront them, willing to talk—if the party agrees to raid the Gnolls with them. When questions turn to the hawks, the Hobgoblins turn hostile. Steel is drawn. Ulrich paralyses one with Hold Person, though both he and Barny take punishing blows. Luthien ends the fight decisively with Sleep, and the rest are swiftly cut down.

In the aftermath, the Bonebreakers recover a staggering haul—jewellery worth roughly 8,000 gold—leaving the cave richer, bloodied, and one step deeper into whatever is truly pulling the strings in the Westmarsh.
