## Session 37 – Drums Beneath the Hills

With the magic still holding their enemies in place, the Bonebreakers press deeper into the cave, following cart tracks that vanish into the dark. They soon stumble upon Kobolds mining by torchlight. Selvar drops them with Sleep; Steve and Akal cut down two, sparing a third for questioning. The terrified creature offers little of value, and is dismissed as the party pushes on.

Dragging the carts forward, they enter a larger chamber where more kobolds toil under the watchful eyes of two hobgoblin overseers. Beyond them, four bugbears lurk near the rear of the cavern. A sharp, brutal fight follows. One bugbear survives long enough for Steve to charm it, and the creature quickly proves talkative. It reveals the truth: a nearby base is stockpiling weapons in preparation for an imminent war.

Seeing the scale of what’s coming together, the Bonebreakers withdraw to the Spider’s Market to rest and resupply. There, rumours confirm their fears — the hobgoblins are actively hiring mercenaries, mustering forces for a fortress not far from the marsh.

Before they can move, gnolls strike the camp. The party repels the attack decisively, and with no more reason to wait, turns their attention toward the fortress itself.

Choosing caution over brute force, they send Rose ahead. Barny cloaks her in invisibility and lifts her into the air, letting her drift silently over the walls. From above and within, she sees the truth laid bare: stockpiles of weapons and armour, hobgoblins everywhere, and in a separate chamber, larger commanders bent over maps — planning something far bigger than a raid.

## Session 38 – The Siege Yet to Come

Rose, still invisible and flying, scouts the hobgoblin fortress by slipping in through a high skylight. The fort is carved into a sheer cliff face amid hills and low mountains, and inside she finds frantic preparation for war. Hobgoblins crowd the halls: a main chamber with soldiers, a forge churning out weapons, and a planning room dominated by a massive map of the Westmarsh and East Agria. Beneath one wall she spots a hawk feather identical to the one recovered when Tobold was taken—clear proof the kidnappings and the army are linked. Unable to find a secret door, she instead sabotages the forge, hurling oil into the furnace and killing several hobgoblins in the blast. As chaos erupts, she slips back to the planning room, steals the invasion maps and documents, and escapes.

Back with the party, Luthien and Selvar translate the papers: they outline a full invasion of Agria, with West Fort as a primary target—and soon. Believing they’ve seen only part of the garrison but unwilling to let the chance slip, the Bonebreakers strike. Ulrich blesses them, Barny puts the outer guards to sleep, and Rose opens the gate from within as the party charges in. Selvar fells the hobgoblins in the main hall with magic, but officers rush in and the fight turns brutal and messy. Through stubborn teamwork—and more than a few close calls—the Bonebreakers prevail, looting gold and powerful arms from the fallen.

Pushing deeper, they catch a crowned hobgoblin leader opening a hidden passage. He flees into a vast hall, revealing the true horror: an enormous invasion force of hobgoblins, orcs, goblins, and even humans, gathered around siege engines and awaiting orders. When the alarm is raised, the party has only seconds. They douse the passage in their last jar of dragon grease, ignite it, and flee—mounting their horses and riding hard back to West Fort.

Commander Valerius listens grimly as they deliver the news of the imminent siege. He asks them to continue searching for the stolen children while he prepares the fort for war. He also brings troubling news from the Mercy: priests have been poisoned, Bishop Arden’s leadership is under scrutiny, and unrest is spreading. Cedric writes urgently to Arden, Ulrich sends a protective crown to ward against poison, and Barny confirms through the crystal ball that the clergy are indeed sick—and that Jeremy has resurfaced near the cliffside fort.

Exhausted but resolute, the Bonebreakers rest in West Fort. They stock up on antitoxins and healing draughts from Dr. Erasmus Vale, identify a potion of flying, and learn he will pay handsomely for rare herbs from the Westmarsh. As night falls, the sense is unmistakable: war is coming, and the clock is already ticking.

## Session 39 – Ashes of the Siege

The Bonebreakers spend a rare quiet night in West Fort before seeking aid at first light. Preparations are swift and purposeful. Steve is loaned a charm-deflecting shield by Mara Ironhand—on the condition he fights for the fort. Rose trades secrets with Gorm the Fence for a deadly necklace. Cedric prays with Sister Aldrith, receiving a sacred text to study, while Luthien and Selvar each secure finely crafted Elven gear. Ulrich arms himself with enchanted plate, the party steadily hardening for what’s to come.

Then word arrives from the Church. Urgent. Grim. Three priests are dead, more are failing, and Bishop Arden pleads for help. Barny confirms the truth through his crystal ball—overhearing Arden’s uncertainty, and his quiet reliance on Cedric—but keeps that detail to himself.

Before the party can act, the alarm bells ring.

From the battlements, the Bonebreakers see it: the army. Hobgoblin ranks stretch across the horizon—archers, infantry, and siege engines dragged forward by ogres—disorganised, but advancing. Worse still, Ulrich spots the sky darken as two dozen giant hawks descend, each carrying goblins to drop into the fort.

The party reacts instantly. Spells ripple through the air—Sleep fells more than half the hawks, sending goblins plummeting to their deaths. Others are blinded, burned, or forced to drop their cargo. The surviving attackers are scattered, and the hawks retreat, screaming back toward the enemy stronghold.

Rather than wait for the siege, the Bonebreakers strike first.

Under cover of magic, they slip out of West Fort and ride hard for the invasion fortress. Steve, rendered invisible and airborne, sabotages the siege engines ahead of the army—cutting ropes, sowing chaos—before rejoining the group as they narrowly evade gnoll patrols.

At the fortress, Akal shrinks and slips inside, raising the portcullis from within. The party enters to find it eerily quiet. Steve scouts ahead and is briefly set upon by bugbears—only for tensions to ease when they recognise him from earlier dealings.

The great hall that once held an army now lies empty.

Beyond, the Bonebreakers discover a long corridor of cells. All are vacant—but the signs are unmistakable. Toys. Chalk drawings. Childlike markings. This was where the kidnapped children were held.

Using the Seer’s Dagger, Barny spies Jeremy deep within the fortress, speaking with Ash—though their exact location remains unclear.

Ulrich’s search reveals a hidden passage, leading the party deeper underground. They move cautiously through corridors and crossroads until they are intercepted by orcs—not hostile, but expectant. The orcs guide them onward.

At last, the party comes face to face with Jeremy… and Ash.

Calm, composed, and utterly in control, Ash acknowledges their interference—and offers something unexpected. A deal. Join the Grey Syndicate, investigate a nearby necropolis, and share any information they uncover. The reward? All treasure they can carry.

The Bonebreakers stand at a crossroads. The enemy has a name now—and an offer.

## Session 40 – Rescue at the End of the Marsh

The Bonebreakers press Ash hard for answers, but she gives them nothing. Every question—about Jeremy, the poisonings, the attacks—meets the same calm denial. The Grey Syndicate, she insists, is merely a “commercial venture.” Her offer stands: investigate a nearby necropolis, share what they find, and take 1,000 gold upfront.

The party fractures. Steve is ready to accept. Selvar and Barny lean toward the deal. Akal is tempted, but wary. Cedric refuses outright—his focus remains on the missing children and the will of Belenus. Even as Luthien suggests playing along for now, Cedric stands firm.

Ash reads the hesitation as refusal.

With a word, she orders their deaths and vanishes through a revolving door before anyone can stop her.

Combat erupts. Webs lock the orcs in place as Ulrich blesses the party. Steel and spell cut them down quickly, but Ash is gone. Cedric fails to force the hidden door, and only after the fighting ends does the party regroup. Jeremy is spared, and under pressure reveals little more—only that the Syndicate is secretive, mercenary, and likely genuine in its offer.

Working together, the Bonebreakers finally force the door open, finding a rough escape tunnel leading out into the wild. Ash has vanished without a trace.

Back inside, they gather what remains—coin from the fallen, and the Syndicate’s documents. The truth becomes clearer: a deliberate campaign to destabilise Agria through poison, fire, and kidnapping. Jeremy insists he played no part in the poisonings—only the arson meant to kill the party.

Locked in, they search for another way through the complex, uncovering a key and finally opening a sealed set of double doors. Beyond lies a vast, foul chamber—thick with feathers and filth. The hawks’ nesting ground.

And there—the children.

Alive.

Cedric moves first, calming and feeding them, while the party ushers them out of the stench-filled chamber. With their rescue complete, the Bonebreakers slip out through a hidden eastern exit and flee into the mountains.

Barny checks the crystal ball—West Fort still stands, though the battlefield is shattered. The enemy army has broken.

After days of careful travel, avoiding the dangers of the marsh, the party returns to West Fort. Commander Valerius greets them with rare approval, taking the children into safety. Rewards are promised—but the news grows darker. More deaths at the cathedral. Sickness spreading. Fires in Ikiria.

The shadow has not lifted.

The party reports everything they’ve learned of the Grey Syndicate, but Barny quietly withholds what he sees through the crystal ball—grave illness among the clergy—his own priorities pulling him back toward the marsh. Cedric, however, remains resolute. He will see the truth with his own eyes.

After resupplying, the Bonebreakers return to Barrow Spa, collect Tess, and claim a hefty reward—24,000 gold—for rescuing the children.

But their respite is brief.

At the Mercy cathedral, an angry mob gathers. When Cedric approaches, they turn on him instantly. Inside, Captain Fardr reveals the truth: the cathedral’s well has been poisoned—and Arden’s poor handling of it has only inflamed tensions.

As Arden steps forward to address the crowd, apologising for his failures, the anger only grows.

It is Akal, of all people, who breaks the moment—scattering gold into the crowd and dispersing them in a storm of bitter murmurs.

## Session 41 – Into the Necropolis

![][image4]

The Bonebreakers examine the cathedral’s poisoned well, and ponder the rumours of plague that continue to drift in from Ikiria. Tobold is still missing, and Ash’s escape remains an open wound.

That night, Barny chooses to sleep alone in the hidden lower level beneath the cathedral. In the dark, Tobold’s voice returns — not promising treasure this time, but warning him not to come down, insisting that all is well and that he is “learning.” Naturally, Barny ignores the warning.

Using the Seer’s Dagger, he stabs Rattius and sends the rat down the spiral staircase while watching through his eyes. What Rattius sees is impossible: blue-lit walls, shifting orientation, moments where descending feels like climbing, and an end point that becomes a beginning the moment he turns around. When Barny tells the others, the party gathers and descends together.

Ulrich casts Detect Magic, and the answer is immediate and overwhelming — the entire place is drenched in arcane energy. Once they pass fully into the strange, inverted geometry below, the whispers finally stop.

At the far end of the upside-down chamber, Frank finds a trapdoor in the ceiling of polished black basalt. Pushing through it, the party emerges into a colossal hall: eight great archways, seven glowing and one sealed, arranged around a central chamber. A giant imperial eagle statue stands watch, two red gemstones glimmering in its eyes. The numerals carved above the arches are ancient imperial marks, older even than those used by the Ramens — relics of the lost empire that once ruled the Westmarsh.

Rose presses one of the eagle’s gemstones. Steve presses the other. The ash-curtains across the archways vanish, and from Arch I, nine skeletons march forth in silence. Ulrich raises his holy symbol and Turns Undead, destroying them in a wave of divine force. The ash-curtains fall once more. The Bonebreakers now realise they are somehow in the famed Necropolis — except it was supposed to be located in Westmarsh.

When the party studies the gates again, each reveals a different fragment of the buried world beyond: flooded halls, incense-scented corridors, ancient boulevards, smoke-stained stairways, construction zones. They choose Arch VII, the one that flickers.

Beyond lies a long-abandoned stonemason’s camp, untouched by rot, lichen, or time. Stone blocks sit half-finished. Tools lie where they were dropped. Plans beneath a mallet show only a portion of a much larger wing: the camp, an unfinished hall, an inverted room, and a chamber labelled Cartographer’s Folly. Sound misbehaves here — footsteps echo too sharply, voices arrive too quickly, and beneath it all is a distant, impossible thump.

In the next room, the party finds a lone figure huddled in the corner: Cornelius Vane, a scholar who says he entered from the Westmarsh six months ago and has been trapped in this cursed wing ever since. By his reckoning, he has only been here eleven days. He asks them, rather meekly, to sit with him. Steve antagonises him; the others oblige.

Cornelius speaks of a civilisation that were master architects and administrators — once lawful, later corrupted by chaos and the worship of chaotic gods. His own maps name places like The Vault, The Twins, and The Chamber. The party offers to guide him out. As they start back, the ceiling caves in behind them, and Steve clears the rubble so they can continue.

They press return to the start room, then delve back deeper. They find an inverted room with an imperial eagle set into the wall and furniture bolted to what should be the ceiling. Frank climbs up, retrieves a scroll case, and lowers a rope so the others can follow. The map inside gives them yet another piece of this impossible place.

In the next chamber, everything is suddenly level again. Smooth walls. A stone plinth. And chained to it, an iron-bound book etched with soul-binding sigils, surrounded by eight numbered iron plates marked with compulsion runes. The door closes behind them of its own accord — and Steve simply opens it again.

He then breaks the chains.

Barny examines the book from a cautious distance, recognising its necrotic nature — souls, binding, compulsion. He reads it anyway, as quickly as possible, and in doing so gains \+1 Intelligence. The text is a treatise on necrotic arts, written by a man named Valedictus.

Beyond that chamber lies the deepest point yet: the Foundation Chamber. Its walls are smooth not by craft, but by some older force. At the centre, in a shallow depression, rests a single skull, once bound by iron stakes and chains that have since been severed. Writing circles the room. Steve throws a rock at the skull, but it bounces harmlessly away. Frank studies the ancient script and realises it is pre-imperial — older than everything else they’ve seen.

It tells of a being that created the world, regretted the act, and has spent all time since trying to undo it. This myth runs against nearly every modern faith. Ulrich attempts to Turn Undead here as well, but nothing answers. No corpse rises. No spirit recoils.

Steve searches the chamber and recovers 200 gold pieces of pre-imperial coinage and a ritual knife of black stone worth 600 gold.

## Session 42 & 43 – Echoes Beneath the Empire

The Bonebreakers pushed deeper into Arch VII, descending once more into the impossible underworld beneath the necropolis. There, they uncovered more of its twisted architecture: strange chambers, warped spaces, and ancient halls where magic seemed to cling to every stone. Sound echoed where it should not, distances felt wrong, and the place itself seemed to resist easy understanding. Much of their time was spent probing these mysteries, testing the strange effects of the necropolis and trying to make sense of the old empire’s buried secrets.

In the midst of this, Rose delivered one of the delve’s defining moments — a sudden, audacious strike that brought down a formidable enemy in a single blow. Even so, the necropolis remained larger, stranger, and more dangerous than the party could fully unravel in one push.

The Bonebreakers eventually withdrew to recover and regroup. During this pause, Steve rode alone to Ikiria, determined to see the truth of the plague with his own eyes. What he found was grim: the sickness was real, spreading, and beyond anything he could meaningfully stop by himself. He turned back for the cathedral, narrowly avoiding bandits on the road and bringing with him only the certainty that the wider crisis was worsening.

Soon after, the party descended again into the necropolis, retracing their way through its haunted geometry and ancient silence. By the end of the missing sessions, they had fought and reasoned their way back toward the deep section marked by the vast claw scars on the walls — and once more, Luthien moved ahead of the others, slipping into the dark to scout what waited beyond.

## Session 44 – Gold Beneath the Beast, Blood Above the Crown

At the end of the Seventh Arch, the Bonebreakers advance cautiously into a broad, natural corridor—its walls scarred with massive claw marks and its air thick with the smell of something ancient. Luthien scouts ahead alone, her boots of elvenkind and cloak rendering her nearly invisible to sound and sight.

To the north, she finds it.

A vast cavern. A slumbering chimera, impossibly old—lion, goat, and dragon heads rising and falling with slow, thunderous breath. Beneath it lies a hoard, compressed gold gathered over centuries. The creature has likely ruled this chamber for two thousand years.

She retreats, then scouts south instead. There, she finds a smaller chamber with a vertical shaft, its walls lined with ladder rungs. Carrying Rose, she leaps upward; Rose climbs sixty feet to a sealed metal grille. Peering through with a mirror, she glimpses a domed chamber above—older stone, strange floor markings, and no visible exits.

The party withdraws. After resting, they return prepared. A pig is acquired. Poisoned. Bound.

Back in the chimera’s domain, the trap is set. Ulrich casts Silence on Rose, Arden Blesses the party, and Barny cloaks Rose in Invisibility. She slips ahead, places the bait beneath the shaft—clearly where the beast is fed—and douses the ground with oil, leaving a lantern to draw its gaze.

In the darkness, she sees it before it sees her—eyes, high above the ground, watching.

The chimera comes.

Ravenous, starving, it devours the pig in seconds. Moments later, it collapses—dead. The poison takes hold swiftly. No battle. No roar. Just silence.

The party moves in. Rose skins the dragon head, hoping to craft armour from it. The hoard is immense: ancient coinage, gemstones, jewellery, relics of multiple ages. Among the finds:

Among the piled wealth, the Bonebreakers uncover relics worthy of legend: a pre-imperial shield claimed by Arden; an imperial spear taken up by Rose; a mysterious magical ring; a manual of strength promising hidden power to whoever studies it; and a red crystal vial whose purpose remains uncertain. Scattered among these treasures lies 6000 ancient gold pieces, likely worth even more to the right buyer.

They haul the treasure out in stages, first to the cathedral, then onward to Barrow Spa. At the Bean Counter, Ruby Sunbeam offers to deposit the gold—but warns the imperial coin may fetch more elsewhere, so the Bonebreakers turn toward Ikiria.

On the road, they encounter a noble procession—fifteen strong, heavily guarded. Rumours stir in memory: merchant killings, false banners, and whispers of royal desperation. Frank dons his persona—Francis Spencer Gray—while Arden adopts his bishop’s authority.

They are brushed aside, until Frank mentions the Grey Syndicate. That changes everything.

The captain confers with the carriage. A decision is made. ‘Kill them.’

The Bonebreakers strike first. Selvar casts Sleep, dropping ten guards instantly. Ulrich holds the captain in place with Hold Person. Luthien webs the drivers, locking the carriage in place. Arden tears open the door and knocks Prince Arthur unconscious with a single, controlled blow.

The aftermath is tense. A fleeing squire is pinned through the leg by Rose’s new spear. Under pressure—and magic—truth begins to spill. Luthien casts Charm Person on Arthur, and what follows is worse than expected.

Arthur is on his way to meet the Grey Khan—an orc, leader of the Grey Syndicate. He seeks guidance… on how to become king. When asked about Princess Agatha, his sister, he answers plainly:

The Grey Khan will deal with her. The merchant attacks? His doing. Disguised as her guards. The truth settles in — this is no distant conspiracy — the Syndicate reaches the throne, and Prince Arthur is already in its grasp.

## Session 45 – The Syndicate’s Silence

The Bonebreakers stand in the uneasy aftermath of their clash with Prince Arthur. The road is littered not with corpses, but with consequences: guards lie sleeping, the captain held by magic, squires wounded or unconscious, and the prince himself—charmed, compliant, and dangerously talkative. Crucially, only a handful have heard his confession. The truth is known… but not yet unleashed.

Before the party can decide their next move, two caravans approach—then, at the sight of the scene, panic and turn tail. Word is already beginning to spread.

Acting quickly, the Bonebreakers try to get ahead of the storm. A terrified young squire, Pell, is sent racing to Commander Smith with a letter explaining everything, Frank pressing gold into his hand to steady his nerves. Arthur, still under Luthien’s influence, is made to order his men into cooperation when they wake, preventing further bloodshed.

Among the prince’s belongings, Frank uncovers something far more dangerous than any blade—a secretary’s ledger detailing meetings with the Grey Syndicate. Proof.

The party withdraws to the Cathedral, where rumours have already outrun them. A shaken caravan reports that the Bonebreakers were slaughtering the prince’s retinue. Captain Fardr meets them in alarm—but Arden deftly smooths the situation, presenting Arthur alive and unharmed. Tension ebbs, though uneasily.

Behind the scenes, contingencies are laid. Frank extracts a quiet oath from Akal: if the party vanishes, the truth goes to the Princess.

With matters temporarily contained, the Bonebreakers move on—first to Barrow Spa, where armour is commissioned, curios purchased, and, oddly, Frank and Arthur begin to form an unexpected rapport. Luthien gifts the prince a ring, revealing it to be one of water-walking—a small, strange gesture in a growing web of politics and betrayal.

From there, they travel to Westfort, taking up in Vex’s warehouse. Through Arthur’s secretary, they attempt to re-establish contact with the Grey Syndicate via Gorm, but the shadows close ranks. Nights pass with nothing—until at last, a brief, silent exchange at the gate… followed by a message: the meeting is cancelled.

The Bonebreakers realise the truth—they’ve been seen with Arthur. Their cover is broken.

With subtlety no longer an option, they turn back toward Westmarsh.

The journey is swift—and violent. Eight ogres ambush them on the road, but the fight is brutally one-sided. Sleep, light, and magic tear through the creatures, though not without cost—one of Arthur’s guards falls in the chaos.

At last, they reach the Spider’s Market, that strange, ancient place where monsters trade beneath unspoken laws: no violence, no broken deals, no loose secrets. The party camps just beyond its edge, resting beneath the uneasy peace of the marsh.

And then—movement. A group of halflings approaches through the dusk. Could it be Tobold?

## Session 46 – The Grey Khan’s Game

On the edge of the Spider’s Market, a new figure finds the Bonebreakers—Micaelis, a disgraced city guard with an almost religious devotion to the spear, seeking to prove its supremacy. He joins them as the party settles into uneasy camp beneath the fragile peace of the marsh. That peace does not last.

In the dead of night, a halfling creeps toward the camp. Arden senses the threat instantly and raises the alarm. Light flares, magic lashes out, and in a chaotic clash Steve is hurled bodily into the intruder by a charmed Ogre. Luthien brings him down, Micaelis strikes, and the party binds him before he can escape. Then they see his face. Tobold. Or is it?

The man is cold, silent, an assassin wearing a dead friend’s face. A pouch of gems and a map to the hobgoblin fortress are found on him, but it is only after gold changes hands that the truth comes out: Tobold is dead, tortured—but unbroken. The impostor was sent to kill the prince’s secretary. The party lets him go as agreed.

The revelation hangs heavy. Even Arthur, under charm, offers little clarity—only that his dealings were with Ash, never the Grey Khan.

By day, the Bonebreakers move within the Spider’s Market itself. Among monsters and mercenaries, they gather rumours: a shattered adventuring party speaks of skeleton patrols and the necropolis entrance to the west—perhaps linked to the one beneath the Cathedral.

Tensions begin to coil tight when Arden openly challenges one of the watching orcs, pressing him about the Grey Syndicate. The orc bristles, warning him to keep his voice down, offering nothing more than the same cold invitation as before: enter the necropolis, or walk away. Everything changes when Prince Arthur’s identity is revealed.

The reaction is immediate. Subtle at first—but unmistakable. More orcs gather. Eyes linger too long. The Bonebreakers feel the weight of attention settle over them. Whatever anonymity they had is gone. Still, a meeting is arranged for the following day. When they return, they do not find a messenger.

They find Ash.

She arrives composed, flanked by two orcs hauling a cart, as if this were any ordinary exchange. Her gaze flicks once to Arthur—lingering just long enough to make it clear she understands exactly what the party has done to him. She wastes no time. The offer is simple: 10,000 gold in exchange for the secretary.

The party pushes back immediately. The secretary is leverage—one of the few pieces they hold—and they are not about to trade him cheaply. The negotiation stretches, tense and careful, both sides probing for weakness. The price climbs. Then Ash shifts the ground beneath them. She claims that the Grey Khan will not be coming, because she is the Grey Khan.

In the end, a deal is struck: 20,000 gold, to be exchanged the following day. Ash turns to leave, the matter seemingly settled, but as the hours pass, it becomes clear she has not gone far at all. She remains within the bounds of the Spider’s Market, somewhere among its shifting crowds and silent watchers.

And so the Bonebreakers make their decision. If they are to act, it must be here—inside the Market itself. Quietly. Cleanly. Without drawing the attention of the countless eyes around them. A silent strike, in a place bound by three unbreakable rules. Break them… and the Market itself will answer.
